    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_reject_root_frames_outside_the_configured_width() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: high_address,
            length: PAGE_SIZE,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let failure =
            match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config()) {
                Err(error) => error,
                Ok(_) => panic!("candidate creation accepted an out-of-range root frame"),
            };
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateCreateErrorKind::RootFrameOutOfRange);
        let frame = failure
            .frame
            .expect("root token is returned on validation failure");
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), high_address);
        allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_mapping_rejects_out_of_width_table_frames_transactionally() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_1000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: high_address,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), 0x10_1000);
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            0xffff_9000_0000_1000,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::TableFrameOutOfRange);
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_walk_rejects_intermediate_tables_without_owned_tokens() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(2);
        let foreign_frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let root_index = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4)[0];
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        memory.foreign_child = Some((root_index, foreign_frame.address()));
        let candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address),
            Err(PageWalkError::Reader(
                CandidatePageTableReadError::UnownedTable
            ))
        );
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        allocator.deallocate(foreign_frame).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_release_failure_retains_owned_frames_for_retry() {
        const TOTAL_FRAMES: usize = 513;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(TOTAL_FRAMES);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let mut remaining_frames: [Option<Frame>; TOTAL_FRAMES - 1] =
            core::array::from_fn(|_| Some(allocator.allocate().unwrap()));
        for index in (1..remaining_frames.len()).step_by(2) {
            allocator
                .deallocate(remaining_frames[index].take().unwrap())
                .unwrap();
        }

        let failure = match candidate.release(&mut allocator) {
            Err(failure) => failure,
            Ok(()) => panic!("release unexpectedly fit a full range table"),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            failure.error,
            CandidateReleaseError::Frame(FrameError::RangeTableFull)
        );
        assert_eq!(failure.candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(failure.candidate.mapping_count(), 0);

        allocator
            .deallocate(remaining_frames[0].take().unwrap())
            .unwrap();
        failure.candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        for frame in remaining_frames.into_iter().flatten() {
            allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), TOTAL_FRAMES as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn active_candidate_rejects_mutation_and_release_until_deactivated() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(4);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
        // SAFETY: This is a synthetic test of the active-state guard; no CPU
        // actually uses the test candidate's root.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        assert!(candidate.is_active());
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(0xffff_9000_0000_1000),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::Active)
        ));

        let failure = candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.error, CandidateReleaseError::ActiveRoot);
        let mut candidate = failure.candidate;
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), root);
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test never installed this root in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn active_owned_mapping_invalidates_before_returning_frame_ownership() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(8);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical_address = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: true,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        candidate.memory.record_events = true;
        // SAFETY: The host backend records invalidations and no hardware CR3 is
        // changed; this tests active API state and ownership ordering only.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        // SAFETY: Synthetic active-root ownership is established above, and the
        // backend's invalidation operation records this leaf address.
        unsafe {
            candidate
                .map_owned_page_active(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
                .unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidation_count, 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidated_pages[0], virtual_address);
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[3],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::PageWrite { value, .. }) if value & 1 != 0
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[4],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::Invalidate { virtual_address })
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address),
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                if translation.physical_address == physical_address
        ));

        // SAFETY: The synthetic root remains the candidate's current test root;
        // unmap invalidates the address before the frame token is returned.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidation_count, 2);
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidated_pages[1], virtual_address);
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[5],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::PageWrite { value: 0, .. })
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[6],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::Invalidate { virtual_address })
        );
        allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        // SAFETY: No real CPU installed this host-test candidate in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_clone_preserves_inherited_entries_and_shared_tables() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let indexes = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4);
        let source_root = 0x8000;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0], 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0] + 1, 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0x9000, indexes[1], 0xa000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xa000, indexes[2], 0xb000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xb000, indexes[3], 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 63));

        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        candidate
            .clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: 0x20_0000,
                leaf_physical_base: 0x20_0000,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: PagePermissions {
                    writable: true,
                    executable: false,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 63),
            })
        );

        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn inherited_large_page_permission_change_splits_and_preserves_cache_type() {
        let total_frames = 16;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let indexes = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4);
        let source_root = 0x8000;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0], 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0x9000, indexes[1], 0xa000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xa000, indexes[2], 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 7) | (1 << 12));
        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        candidate
            .clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root)
            .unwrap();

        candidate
            .set_inherited_page_permissions(
                &mut allocator,
                virtual_address,
                0x20_1000,
                PagePermissions {
                    writable: false,
                    executable: false,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
            )
            .unwrap();
        let protected = match candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("split mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(protected.physical_address, 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(protected.page_size, PAGE_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(
            protected.permissions,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(protected.pat_index, 4);

        let neighbor = match candidate.walk(virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("neighbor mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(neighbor.physical_address, 0x20_2000);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.page_size, PAGE_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.permissions.writable, true);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.permissions.executable, true);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.pat_index, 4);

        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        candidate
            .clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root)
            .unwrap();

            .set_inherited_page_permissions(

        };
        assert_eq!(protected.physical_address, 0x4040_1000);

    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_clone_rejects_invalid_large_page_entries_and_clears_root() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(4);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let source_root = 0x8000;
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let root_index = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4)[0];
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(source_root, root_index, 0x9000 | 0x3 | (1 << 7));
        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root),
            Err(CandidateCloneError::InvalidEntry {
                level: 4,
                index: root_index,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent {
                level: PageLevel::Pml4,
            }
        );
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_require_nx_and_report_unmapped_pages() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(2);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let invalid = CandidatePageTables::new(
            &mut allocator,
            &mut memory,
            PageWalkConfig {
                nx_enabled: false,
                ..four_level_walk_config()
            },
        );
        let error = match invalid {
            Err(error) => error,
            Ok(_) => panic!("candidate creation unexpectedly accepted disabled NX"),
        };
        assert_eq!(error.cause, CandidateCreateErrorKind::InvalidConfiguration);
        assert_eq!(error.frame, None);

        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(0xffff_9000_0000_1000),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::NotMapped)
        );
        assert!(candidate.release(&mut allocator).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_borrowed_acpi_without_owning_its_frame() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let acpi_physical = 0x20_0000;
        let acpi_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: acpi_physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = acpi_map
            .validate_acpi_span(acpi_physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            acpi_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map - 3);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: acpi_physical,
                leaf_physical_base: acpi_physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: acpi_physical | 1 | (1 << 63),
            })
        );
        let duplicate_virtual = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            duplicate_virtual.cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::MappingAlreadyPresent
        );
        let other_virtual = virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE;
        let other_mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            other_virtual,
            acpi_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let duplicate_physical = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, other_mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            duplicate_physical.cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::PhysicalPageAlreadyMapped
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::OwnershipMismatch)
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        // SAFETY: This synthetic test checks the inactive-only guard; the CPU
        // never installs the candidate's root.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_acpi_page(virtual_address),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::Active)
        );
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test never installed this root in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.unmap_acpi_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_explicit_uncacheable_mmio_without_frame_ownership() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let mmio_physical = 0xfee0_0000;
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_d000_0000_0000;
        let mmio_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: 0x10_0000,
            length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mmio_span = mmio_map
            .validate_mmio_page(mmio_physical, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            mmio_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            permissions,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let attributes = super::SelectedCacheAttributes {
            physical_start: mmio_physical,
            physical_end: mmio_physical + PAGE_SIZE,
            pat_index: 3,
            effective_type: EffectiveMemoryType::Uncacheable,
        };
        let before = allocator.free_frames();
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test treats this as a device page and never
        // dereferences it; the API's map authorization, range, permissions, and
        // UC requirements apply.
        unsafe {
            candidate
                .map_mmio_page(&mut allocator, mmio_span, mapping, attributes)
                .unwrap()
        };
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), before - 3);
        let translation = match candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("MMIO mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(translation.physical_address, mmio_physical);
        assert_eq!(translation.permissions, permissions);
        assert_eq!(translation.pat_index, 3);
        assert_eq!(translation.raw_leaf_entry & (1 << 63), 1 << 63);

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_mmio_page(virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::NotMapped)
        );
        candidate.unmap_mmio_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_reject_invalid_borrowed_acpi_mappings() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(8);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let physical = 0x20_0000;
        let other_physical = 0x30_0000;
        let memory_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE * 8,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: other_physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = memory_map
            .validate_acpi_span(physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let writable = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: true,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = writable
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let failure = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, writable, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping);
        let executable = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                executable: true,
                ..KERNEL_READ_ONLY
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let executable_attributes = executable
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, executable, executable_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        let user = validate_mapping_range(
            0x4000,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                user_accessible: true,
                ..KERNEL_READ_ONLY
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let user_attributes = user
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, user, user_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        let wrong_span = memory_map
            .validate_acpi_span(other_physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let read_only = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let read_only_attributes = read_only
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, wrong_span, read_only, read_only_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn borrowed_acpi_mapping_rolls_back_new_tables_on_frame_exhaustion() {
        let total_frames = 3;

            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())

                base: physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },

        .unwrap();
        let span = map
            .validate_acpi_span(physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0xffff_9000_0000_1000,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();

            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_unmap_and_release_owned_frames() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), Some(root));
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0x0000_4000_0000_1000;
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        };
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(&frame, virtual_address, permissions);

        candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: physical,
                leaf_physical_base: physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: physical | 0x3 | (1 << 2) | (1 << 63),
            })
        );

        let duplicate_frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let (duplicate_mapping, duplicate_attributes) =
            candidate_mapping(&duplicate_frame, virtual_address, permissions);
        let free_before_duplicate = allocator.free_frames();
        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(
                &mut allocator,
                duplicate_frame,
                duplicate_mapping,
                duplicate_attributes,
            )
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::MappingAlreadyPresent);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_duplicate);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();

        let returned = candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(returned.address(), physical);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent {
                level: PageLevel::Pt,
            }
        );
        allocator.deallocate(returned).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_arithmetic_overflow_and_writable_executable_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                0,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );

        let writable_executable = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: true,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x2000, PAGE_SIZE, writable_executable, Some(52), 48),
            Err(MappingError::WritableExecutable)
        );
    }

# Unix-like process and syscall direction

**Status: design direction only. No process, syscall, or userland support is implemented.**

Rustix aims to expose a small, versioned syscall surface that can support Unix-like processes and tools. The kernel must own this interface rather than inherit an ABI accidentally from a bootloader or emulator.

## Proposed compatibility principles

- Processes have independent virtual address spaces and explicit lifecycle states.
- File descriptors are per-process integer handles to kernel-managed objects; descriptor inheritance, close-on-exec, duplication, and sharing semantics must be specified together.
- Syscalls use one documented error convention and stable numeric identifiers. New operations must not silently repurpose old numbers.
- Arguments crossing privilege boundaries are copied or validated using narrowly scoped helpers. User memory is never dereferenced as a trusted Rust reference.
- Blocking, interruption, cancellation, and restart behavior are explicit for each syscall class.
- A compatibility layer (for example, POSIX-shaped libc behavior) remains separate from internal kernel APIs.

## Initial x86_64 entry design (Milestone 4; not implemented)

The first single-vCPU user-mode slice will enter the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated IDT interrupt gate at DPL 3 and return with `IRETQ`. This intentionally avoids `SYSCALL`/`SYSRET`, `STAR`/`LSTAR`/`FMASK`, and `SWAPGS` state transitions in the first userspace path. It is a provisional architecture decision, not a published or implemented syscall ABI.

- **Vector ownership:** `0x80` is currently inside Rustix's device-vector allocation range (`0x20..=0xef`). Before installing the user-callable gate, reserve it from `InterruptVectorAllocator` and install a dedicated syscall stub rather than the generic device-IRQ stub. The gate must be an interrupt gate, so maskable interrupts are disabled on entry before Rust dispatch.
- **Selectors:** the current GDT uses `0x08` for kernel code, `0x10` for kernel data, and `0x18` for the two-slot TSS descriptor. Append ring-3 data and code descriptors after the TSS without moving existing selectors: user data selector `0x2b` and user code selector `0x33` (GDT indexes 5 and 6 with RPL 3). The user code descriptor must be 64-bit code; the data selector is loaded into user `SS` on return. These values are a design target and must be asserted by the GDT implementation/tests before use.
- **Privilege stack:** a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt uses `TSS.RSP0`; it must point to the top of the current process's mapped, writable kernel-entry stack before user execution is resumed. The existing TSS points to one static bootstrap ring-0 stack, so it is not sufficient for processes. On this single-vCPU design the scheduler must update `RSP0` whenever it selects a process to run in user mode. A future SMP design needs per-CPU TSS and entry-stack state.
- **Entry frame and state:** the assembly stub must preserve the complete user register state and construct a separately specified syscall frame; it must not assume the existing fatal-exception frame is interchangeable. Kernel code must run with the direction flag clear. Preserve user x87/SSE state across kernel handling; AVX remains disabled under the current CPU-state policy. Do not form Rust references from user pointers.
- **Initial register convention:** `RAX` carries the syscall number; arguments use `RDI`, `RSI`, `RDX`, `R10`, `R8`, and `R9`; `RAX` carries the result. This is only a proposed register convention. It becomes stable only together with ABI version discovery, syscall numbers, errors, and transfer semantics below.
- **Return validation:** use `IRETQ`, not `SYSRET`. Before returning, validate that the saved `CS` and `SS` are exactly the ring-3 selectors, `RIP` and `RSP` are canonical and within the process's executable/code and stack regions respectively, and `RFLAGS` contains no privileged or unsupported bits. Construct a safe flags value rather than echoing user-controlled flags. A malformed frame terminates the process with a reported status; never attempt the return and rely on a ring-0 `#GP` to catch it.
- **NMI and interrupt policy:** no GS-base swap is needed on this entry path. An NMI can still arrive during entry; the current NMI/exception path is fatal-only, and this design does not claim to recover from it. Keep that behavior explicit until user-origin exception/NMI policy is implemented and tested. Ordinary maskable IRQs may resume only after the entry state and scheduler ownership are consistent.

This design depends on a process-owned address space that maps the syscall entry/return code, IDT, GDT, TSS, and the active kernel stack safely. No Ring 3 execution should be enabled until the address-space implementation is reviewed and validated.

### Process address spaces (design; not implemented)

Use a separate four- or five-level root per process. Each process root owns its root page, all lower-half intermediate tables, and every user leaf frame. Keep the current kernel address-space owner alive for the lifetime of every process root. Copy only upper-half top-level entries from that owner into each process root; these entries are non-owning references to shared kernel subtrees, not deep copies, and must never be released by a process teardown. Do not copy lower-half entries from the kernel root.

Before publishing a shared kernel subtree, validate its page-table structure and physical bounds and reject any present entry with the user/supervisor bit set at any level. Shared kernel mappings therefore remain supervisor-only regardless of the process-owned user mappings. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.

The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. Before releasing a process root or any of its user frames, switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate the local non-global translations; keep the shared kernel owner alive. Do not add PCID or SMP teardown/shootdown behavior implicitly: those require a separate design.

The current `CandidatePageTables` deep-clones the inherited hierarchy, tracks all cloned table frames as owned, holds an exclusive mutable borrow of one memory backend, and does not provide shared-subtree ownership. It is not itself the process-address-space abstraction. Implement the shared-root policy in a distinct owner/handle API that can safely support multiple process roots without aliasing mutable backend references. Until that implementation and its negative tests exist, these paragraphs are a design contract only.

## ABI decisions still required before exposing calls

1. ABI version discovery and compatibility guarantees.
2. Error encoding and a complete initial syscall-number allocation.
3. Pointer/length validation, partial reads/writes, and copy-fault behavior.
4. Process creation and execution semantics, including file actions and inherited descriptors.
5. Signal-like asynchronous delivery, interruption, and restart semantics.
6. Time, clocks, and structure layout rules.

## Suggested first user-visible slice

After address spaces, scheduler, and storage primitives exist, implement a controlled `init` process with a small syscall subset: process exit, read/write through descriptors, open/close, and wait. Add end-to-end tests for invalid pointers, partial transfers, descriptor lifetime, process exit status, and ABI version negotiation before describing it as Unix-compatible.

# Memory-management direction

## What exists now

`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation/classification, canonical-address boundaries, physical-width bounds, HHDM range arithmetic, and page-rounded ACPI span authorization. `MemoryMap::validate_acpi_span` accepts at most 64 KiB of requested ACPI bytes and validates the entire 4 KiB-rounded physical extent against contiguous ACPI-reclaimable/NVS regions; this is metadata only, not a mapping or dereference grant. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.

`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and coalesces adjacent free ranges. The boot path additionally subtracts the validated kernel-image and boot-stack physical spans (`from_memory_map_excluding`) so a loader mislabeling them as usable cannot cause the allocator to hand out own-kernel pages. The ownership contract assumes one allocator instance per physical map: within that instance, each eligible frame is owned either by its free-range table or by a non-copyable `Frame` token while allocated. The public constructor does not enforce unique instances, so callers must not initialize multiple allocators for the same physical map; the boot path retains one allocator in `BootInfo`. `allocate` returns `None` when no free frame remains. `deallocate` consumes the token only on success; on any error, including free-range-table exhaustion, it returns a `DeallocationError` containing the original token and leaves allocator state unchanged. The range tables each have a fixed `MAX_FRAME_RANGES` capacity, so fragmentation can prevent a frame from being returned until nearby ranges coalesce. The active cloned page-table hierarchy owns its page-table frames; the frame allocator is otherwise not yet a general-purpose virtual-memory service.

`Frame::address()` is a physical address value, not a dereferenceable pointer and not a proof that the frame is mapped. CPU diagnostics now read `CR4.LA57` to report the active linear-address width (48 or 57 bits) and query `CPUID.80000008H` for physical and maximum linear-address widths when available. Boot-protocol pointers are checked against the active width, with host tests for 48- and 57-bit canonical boundaries. These facts do not prove that any physical address is mapped.

`src/paging.rs` contains host-tested mapping and cache policy plus a bounded candidate-root builder. The CR3 decoder validates physical-address width and reserved bits and interprets its low 12 bits according to active `CR4.PCIDE`; it does not dereference the root. The mapping-range validator requires known physical width, checked aligned bounds, canonical virtual endpoints in one canonical half, and rejects writable-executable permissions. It can encode one 4 KiB leaf PTE with supervisor/user and write permissions, NX when EFER.NXE is confirmed, and a bounded PAT index. `PatLayout` parses supplied `IA32_PAT` values and selects WB, UC, or WC indexes. `MtrrMemoryType`, `VariableMtrr`, `FixedMtrrRanges`, and `MtrrLayout` resolve address-specific MTRR types, including fixed-range priority and defined variable-overlap rules; undefined overlaps fail closed. `MtrrRegisters::validated_layout` validates captured capability/default-type bits, register counts and fixed-range presence, WC support, and variable-mask shape/alignment before producing an owned layout. Rustix supports contiguous power-of-two variable masks and explicitly rejects unsupported discontinuous masks. The layout combines address-specific MTRR type and PAT selection according to Intel SDM Table 11-7 only when `CR0.CD` and `CR0.NW` are clear. Host tests cover all 30 documented MTRR/PAT pairs and malformed inputs. A pure range selector chooses an index only when its effective type is uniform throughout all fixed/variable MTRR boundaries in an aligned extent; selected attributes remain bound to that physical extent. The selector itself does not inspect PTEs, aliases, or frame ownership. Boot reads CR0 without modifying it, validates captured MTRR/PAT state, and reports a diagnostic PA 0 resolution; this does not assert the live PTE's type. MTRR capture is bounded to 32 variable pairs and rejects excess capacity without partial state.

`CandidatePageTables` owns a separate root, bounded to 32 table frames and 256 explicitly mapped leaf records. Ordinary owned leaves require allocator-issued `Frame` tokens; a separate bounded ACPI path accepts only one read-only, supervisor, NX 4 KiB page contained in a `ValidatedAcpiSpan` and never transfers ownership of that physical page. Both paths require NXE, support four- and five-level paths, and hold one exclusive mutable borrow of the unsafe memory backend so prepared handles cannot be mixed across backends. Borrowed ACPI mappings can only be installed and removed while the candidate is inactive. The boot-only ACPI reader performs temporary CR3 switches to read validated pages and removes them before permanent activation. The default boot path clones the complete reachable Limine hierarchy, hardens kernel HHDM aliases to text/rodata R/NX and data RW/NX while preserving PAT bits, verifies critical translations, activates the cloned CR3, and retains the candidate tokens for the active root's lifetime. The CR3 transition invalidates the active PCID and toggles CR4.PGE when enabled; the same invalidation is used if verification restores the inherited root. General candidate mutation and release are rejected while active, but narrow owned-page active map/unmap operations are supported under the single-CPU, IF-disabled contract and invalidate the local TLB before ownership is returned. Host tests cover transactional rollback and ownership; `just active-map-smoke` validates active mapping, access, invalidation, and reclamation in QEMU. The type never writes CR3. The HHDM adapter derives table pointers only from complete allocator-owned `Usable` frames through checked arithmetic.

The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe reads the inherited root and follows paths for every page in kernel text/rodata/data and the requested stack span. The transition clones every reachable present table and preserves leaf mappings, then rewrites and validates the kernel-image HHDM aliases. The kernel and HHDM aliases retain the same PAT index; MTRR state is unchanged. This is not a fresh address-space policy or a hardware-level exhaustive inventory, and it does not reclaim the inherited root or bootloader memory.

The effective-type resolver follows [Intel SDM Vol. 3A §11.5.2.2, Table 11-7](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/671447/325384-sdm-vol-3abcd.pdf), which applies when normal caching is enabled (`CR0.CD=0`, `CR0.NW=0`). Its footnotes distinguish UC selected by an MTRR from UC selected by a page-table entry (the latter involves cache snooping and aliasing concerns); they also identify combinations that older manual editions called undefined but current processors supporting both PAT and MTRRs resolve as shown. The resolver does not cover legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations outside that table.

The requested Limine base revision is 3. Its protocol maps only `Usable`, `BootloaderReclaimable`, `ExecutableAndModules`, and `Framebuffer` memory-map regions into the HHDM; reserved, ACPI, bad, and unknown regions are not in that mapping set. HHDM mappings use at least 4 KiB granularity and may cover page-aligned bytes beyond unaligned region boundaries. Limine's inherited HHDM mappings are supervisor RWX, normally write-back cached, with framebuffer mappings write-combining when PAT is available. Before activating the cloned root, Rustix splits inherited huge pages where needed and changes the kernel image HHDM aliases to the matching R/NX or RW/NX policy while retaining PAT bits. The rest of the HHDM remains inherited; an HHDM offset is not a blanket physical-memory access grant. See the [Limine base revision 3 protocol](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine-protocol/blob/trunk/PROTOCOL.md#base-revision-3) and its memory-layout/caching sections.

The boot snapshot rejects physical map ranges beyond the reported CPUID physical-address width when available. For base-revision-3 HHDM-mapped types it validates page-rounded physical spans, checked `offset + address` arithmetic, and canonical endpoints in the active linear-address width. These checks are metadata, not proof that loader pointers are readable. Arbitrary physical access is not permitted: validated ACPI pages use the bounded read-only/NX reader; HHDM table access is limited to checked full-frame paths. Rustix-owned mappings should be non-executable by default; MMIO requires an explicit device range and cache policy, and guard regions must remain unmapped. The APIC MMIO validator rejects every known memory-map class except `Reserved` and `Unknown`; unreported ranges remain dependent on validated platform data. The active clone owns its page-table frames but leaves inherited leaf frames and the old root unreclaimed. The global heap begins with a 256 KiB BSS arena and can demand-map up to 1 MiB of allocator-backed pages in its reserved virtual range. Its IRQ-save lock prevents local interrupt reentrancy, but allocation remains forbidden in IRQ/exception handlers. Bootstrap exceptions remain fatal, while selected maskable IRQs are enabled only after APIC routes and handlers are ready.

## Active-root preservation and remaining limits

The transition clones the complete reachable inherited hierarchy rather than building a clean address space. It preserves all reachable present leaves and non-present entries, owns each cloned intermediate table, and fails closed on malformed entries, unsupported page sizes, cross-level table aliases, or fixed-capacity exhaustion. Kernel text/rodata/data HHDM aliases are then adjusted to avoid writable-executable aliases. Limine's original root and leaf frames remain intact.

- **Kernel ELF image:** `linker.ld` places `.text`, `.rodata`, `.limine_requests`, `.data`, `.bss`, and `.got` in three `PT_LOAD` segments: RX text, read-only rodata, and RW data/BSS. It exports `__kernel_start` and `__kernel_end` around the complete loadable image, plus page-aligned bounds for each segment. `BootInfo` checks that Limine's reported virtual base matches the linker start, validates ordered contiguous segment bounds covering the rounded image, derives corresponding half-open physical ranges from the executable physical base with checked arithmetic, and validates canonical virtual and reported physical address widths. The release ELF and QEMU runtime report both showed the three aligned ranges on 2026-10-21. The RX, R/NX, and RW/NX labels describe the linker segment intent; these are linker/boot metadata, not proof that the inherited page tables map every page or enforce those permissions, nor proof that loader pointers are readable. The memory-map `ExecutableAndModules` entries remain illustrative, not an authoritative kernel-image extent.
- **Active stack and `BootInfo`:** The assembly `_start` shim captures Limine's entry `RSP` before any Rust prologue. Under the SysV entry convention the synthetic return slot occupies 8 bytes, so `RSP + 8` is the exclusive stack top. Rustix requests a 256 KiB Limine stack and requires the stack-size response; `BootInfo` records and validates that requested span through the HHDM, including its `BootloaderReclaimable` backing. The loader may allocate more, and no guard page is inferred. QEMU transition tests walk all 64 requested stack pages.
- **Kernel static data:** `RAM_FILESYSTEM`, GDT, IDT, TSS, the ring-0 stack, and double-fault IST stack are static BSS/data in the kernel image. Exception entry also requires the handler code and the TSS/IDT references to remain mapped. Preserve the complete relevant data/BSS pages and stack pages.
- **Limine request data:** request records are in the kernel's writable `.limine_requests` segment. Response objects and the memory-map pointer array are bootloader-reclaimable; `capture_boot_information` copies the values used later, and the shell does not retain those pointers. Keep them mapped until the copy and validation finish; any later reclaim must be explicit rather than reclaiming the whole bootloader-reclaimable class.
- **Inherited page tables:** Limine places its page tables in bootloader-reclaimable memory, but their layout is unspecified. `BootInfo` captures raw CR3 and validates the decoded root address and active low-bit mode. The default boot path clones all reachable page-table pages into allocator-owned frames and preserves all leaf entries, then changes only the kernel-image HHDM alias permission bits while retaining cache attributes. It verifies kernel segments, the requested stack span, and the candidate-root HHDM alias before switching; afterward it verifies CR3 and the critical paths again. The inherited root and its backing pages remain untouched and are not reclaimed.
- **Devices:** COM1 uses x86 port I/O and needs no MMIO virtual mapping. Rustix does not currently request or use a framebuffer. Any future framebuffer or device-register mapping needs an explicit physical range and cache policy.

## Permissions and cache policy of the active clone

The active root preserves Limine's inherited kernel virtual mappings and their cache attributes. Before switching, Rustix requires NXE and enforces the linker permissions for every kernel-image HHDM alias: text and rodata are read-only/NX, and data/BSS/GOT are RW/NX. This prevents writable-executable aliases without discarding the HHDM alias. Huge-page leaves are split as necessary; unaffected entries retain their mappings and PAT/MTRR effective types. The remainder of the HHDM and all non-kernel aliases remain as Limine supplied them, so this is not yet a comprehensive Rustix mapping policy.

Preserve the inherited PAT/MTRR configuration during the first transition. The boot report validates captured registers and computes a diagnostic effective type from the active PAT/MTRR values under normal caching. A separate pure selector can choose an index whose effective type remains uniform across an aligned physical range; the selector itself does not inspect PTEs or aliases. The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe now compares effective types of the inherited kernel and HHDM aliases for kernel-image pages, but it is not a full alias inventory. The pure combination follows Intel SDM Table 11-7; it is not a generic rule for legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations. The active transition retains the inherited PAT and MTRR state and changes no cache-selection bits. The page-table split copies large-page PAT selection to the equivalent 4 KiB/2 MiB entries. Future MMIO mappings must still use explicit device ranges and a verified cache policy; do not infer MMIO from generic reserved memory-map entries. COM1 uses port I/O and requires no MMIO mapping.

Do not use huge pages in the first root; add them only when physical coverage, permissions, and cache attributes are uniform across the entire huge-page extent. Future Rustix-owned downward-growing stacks should have at least one 4 KiB unmapped guard page below them. The Limine bootstrap stack has no known guard, so none may be assumed there.

Never modify Limine's active page tables in place. `src/paging.rs` builds an owned clone in allocator-issued frames, can split inherited large pages to update leaf permissions, and supports transactional 4 KiB map/unmap operations before activation. The default boot path validates critical translations and kernel alias permissions, switches CR3 while invalidating stale global translations via a CR4.PGE toggle when needed, verifies the active root, and retains its frame tokens for the active lifetime. The inherited root and backing memory remain intact. This preserves inherited mappings rather than constructing a new address space; broader mapping inventory, non-kernel permission policy, reclamation, and a general mapping service remain future work.

## Planned memory layers

1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
2. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; table and leaf mappings use allocator-issued tokens. The active mapping smoke validates one owned page's map/access/unmap/reclamation path.
3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix runs on an active clone of Limine's hierarchy and hardens kernel-image HHDM aliases. Narrow active owned-page map/unmap operations invalidate the local TLB; this is not a clean-room address-space policy or general MMIO subsystem.
4. **Heap:** a 256 KiB BSS arena with 128 allocation records is backed by a bounded, demand-mapped extension of up to 1 MiB. Host tests and QEMU cover growth, reuse, exhaustion, and failed growth. The global allocator uses an IRQ-save spin lock, but allocation remains prohibited in interrupt context so handlers stay bounded and allocation-free.
5. **Process address spaces (planned):** use private lower-half page-table paths and user frames with shared, supervisor-only upper-half kernel subtrees. The kernel mapping owner outlives every process root; process teardown frees only its private tables and frames after switching away and invalidating translations. Define copy-in/copy-out helpers and never treat user pointers as kernel references. This sharing policy is documented but not implemented.

## Invariants to preserve

- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
- Only complete frames in validated `Usable` regions enter the allocator; the first MiB remains reserved. Firmware and loader-reclaimable regions are not silently promoted to free memory.
- Under the single-allocator-per-physical-map contract, a frame is represented by one allocator-free range or one caller-owned, non-copyable `Frame` token. Only a successful `deallocate` transfers the token back to the allocator; errors return the token and leave allocator ranges and accounting unchanged. The current public constructor relies on callers to enforce unique allocator instances.
- `allocate` returns `None` on frame exhaustion. Metadata-capacity exhaustion is an explicit error, never silent loss of a frame.
- A `Frame` address is physical, not directly dereferenceable. HHDM translation and table access are limited to checked full-frame token-based paths that rely on Limine's documented mapping contract. Candidate mutations are allowed only before activation and only in owned tables. The active cloned root retains its ownership tokens and rejects mutation/release until an explicit, reviewed CR3 transition away from it.
- Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables. User-accessible leaf mappings must stay in the lower canonical half; the upper half is reserved for supervisor mappings.
- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, exhaustion, and unchanged state/ownership on failure.

The active root is a full clone of Limine's reachable hierarchy with kernel HHDM alias W^X hardening, not a clean-room Rustix address space. Heap growth is bounded to a fixed virtual reservation and 1 MiB of frame-backed pages. Broader alias/MMIO coverage, frame reclamation, and physical-hardware validation remain outstanding.

# Rustix roadmap

This roadmap describes an incremental path from the current bare-metal kernel to a useful Unix-like operating system. It is a dependency plan, not a schedule or a claim of compatibility. Features become current only after the implementation, tests, and exit criteria below agree.

## How to read status

- A checked box means the source/design work exists; it does **not** imply the code compiled, linked, booted, or passed an integration test.
- A milestone is not complete until its stated exit criteria are met and the evidence is recorded.
- Hardware work needs target build and emulator evidence. Host tests cannot validate privileged instructions, bootloader pointers, page tables, device I/O, or exception-entry assembly.
- Future work is intentionally not represented by placeholder APIs or dummy implementations.

## Current status

- **Milestone 0: local exit criteria met from a clean detached worktree; hosted CI observed.** On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 from both the working tree and a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory. On 2026-11-06, GitHub Actions run [#5](https://github.com/JustEthanCodes/rustix/actions/runs/42288095710) completed successfully on `dev` at `770f9c742dd07a00f6b53274ea05a1eca010d146`; its `kernel-and-boot-smoke` job ran `just verify`. This verifies hosted CI on that remote commit, not today’s uncommitted changes.
- **Milestone 1: validation criteria met for the current Limine path.** The bounded boot snapshot, memory-range classification, and CPUID reporting were covered by host tests and QEMU reporting; the Limine pointer-readability trust boundary remains explicit.
- **Milestone 2: local exit criteria met on 2026-10-24; hosted CI observed, physical-hardware validation pending.** The boot path owns and activates a clone of Limine's reachable page-table hierarchy, preserves inherited mappings, hardens kernel HHDM aliases to R/NX or RW/NX while retaining PAT attributes, invalidates stale translations on CR3 transitions, and retains table-frame tokens. `just verify`, `just frame-smoke`, and `just fault-smoke` passed after final review; QEMU exercised the active-PCID/CR3 invalidation path with CR4.PGE clear. The PGE-toggle path is statically reviewed but was not exercised by this QEMU configuration. The successful 2026-11-06 hosted `just verify` run covers the published Milestone 2 state, but not today's uncommitted changes. Broad mapping policy, reclamation, IRQ-safe allocation, and physical-hardware validation remain outside this milestone's completed scope.
- **Milestone 3: single-vCPU exit criteria met locally on 2026-11-13; hosted CI and physical-hardware validation remain pending.** `just verify` passed with 130 host tests, target check/build, BIOS and OVMF boot smokes, active-map/TLB invalidation, IRQ-save lock checks, timer preemption of non-yielding workers with x87/SSE state preservation, cooperative wait/input behavior, and UART/PS/2 IRQ wakeup. SMP and physical-hardware validation remain deferred. See the evidence and limits below. **Milestones 4 and later: planned.** There is no ARM64 platform support, userspace, syscall ABI, persistent filesystem, GUI, or networking stack.

## Dependency path

```text
Reliable boot
    -> validated boot state
    -> owned mappings + frame allocation + heap + fault diagnostics
    -> timer/IRQ model + scheduler + IRQ-safe locking + timer preemption
    -> isolated processes + syscall ABI
    -> M5a PCI/DMA + block I/O + read-only/basic VFS
    -> M5b writable filesystem + permissions + platform services
    -> userland utilities
    -> graphical terminal and other optional services
```

Some device-driver work can proceed in parallel after the core ownership, locking, and testing rules exist. It must not bypass them with direct, unreviewed hardware access.

## Milestone 3 — IRQs, time, and kernel scheduling (DONE locally; single-vCPU, SMP deferred)

Do not enable interrupts as a side effect of installing exception gates. IRQ delivery needs its own controller, acknowledgement, masking, ownership, and synchronization design.

### Implementation and remaining work

The current source includes host-tested bounded ACPI parsing and span authorization, a boot-only read-only/NX ACPI reader that copies MADT data into owned state, xAPIC/I/O APIC routing, allocated IRQ dispatch and acknowledgement, a PIT timer, a single-vCPU scheduler with cooperative waits and timer preemption, guarded thread stacks, bounded frame-backed heap growth, and interrupt-driven UART/PS/2 queues. `IrqSpinLock` saves/disables local interrupts and restores the prior IF state; the heap uses it, while scheduler mutations are serialized by local interrupt masking. Timer IRQ assembly saves x87/SSE state before Rust dispatch, and context switches preserve per-context FXSAVE state; AVX/XSAVE remains disabled. On 2026-11-13, `just verify` passed with 130 host tests and BIOS/OVMF coverage for active mapping, timer preemption/FPU state, locks, cooperative waits, and input. SMP is not part of this completed single-vCPU slice.

**Ring 3 prerequisite gate:** the single-vCPU IRQ-safe locking and timer-preemption prerequisites in this milestone are now implemented and validated. This only establishes scheduler progress and local interrupt-safe locking; it does not provide user/kernel isolation, safe syscall entry/return, per-process kernel stacks, or any other Milestone 4 guarantee.

- [x] Use the existing single-vCPU QEMU `q35` configuration with the local APIC and MADT-described I/O APIC; keep legacy PIC routing masked. OVMF smokes observed timer and device IRQ delivery.
- [x] Read bounded ACPI tables through the validated read-only/NX path. The reader checks table bounds/signatures/checksums and copies the required MADT data into owned state; host tests cover malformed tables and span authorization, and OVMF reports the copied MADT.
- [x] Parse the selected machine's MADT topology and interrupt-source overrides. Host parser tests and OVMF boot cover the data used by APIC routing; FADT/HPET/MCFG work remains limited to this milestone's needs.
- [x] Add fixed-capacity IRQ vector ownership, masked-first controller routes, dispatch, spurious/unexpected-vector handling, and EOI. OVMF observed timer IRQ delivery and acknowledgement; input routes are also tested.
- [x] Route an approximately 100 Hz 8254 PIT through the I/O APIC and maintain atomic monotonic ticks. Host tests cover divisor and elapsed-time arithmetic, including fractional-tick rounding drift; OVMF verifies live timer delivery and EOI. Wall-clock time remains separate and is not provided.
- [x] Add bounded wait queues, cooperative sleep/wakeup, and event handoff; host scheduler tests and OVMF `thread-smoke` cover wakeup and timed sleep.
- [x] Establish IRQ-safe lock primitives and broader context-specific locking rules before enabling timer preemption. `src/sync.rs` provides an IRQ-save spin lock that restores the prior RFLAGS.IF state; the heap uses it, while scheduler policy changes mask local interrupts and do not hold a lock across context switches. IRQ handlers remain allocation-free and do not acquire the heap lock. Host tests and the OVMF thread smoke validate lock operations and both enabled/disabled IF restoration.
- [x] Implement owned-frame active map/unmap with explicit mapping/cache policy, transactional rollback, and local TLB invalidation. Host tests cover failure rollback; `active-map-smoke` passed live mapping, access, invalidation, and reclamation in QEMU.
- [x] Extend the 256 KiB bootstrap heap with a bounded 1 MiB frame-backed, demand-mapped region. Host tests cover growth, reuse, and failed growth; `thread-smoke` observed bootstrap exhaustion, growth, and reuse.
- [x] Keep allocator operations out of IRQ/exception handlers; handlers use bounded, allocation-free work, and the heap contract explicitly forbids IRQ-context allocation. The IRQ-save heap lock prevents local interrupt reentrancy, but does not make allocation appropriate in handlers. Exhaustion is fallible at the allocator boundary.
- [x] Keep bootloader-reclaimable and ACPI memory, the active bootstrap stack, and Limine's inherited page-table root reserved; the active cloned root retains its owned table frames and does not reclaim the old root or inherited leaf frames.
- [x] Add single-vCPU cooperative threads with owned guarded stacks, lifecycle, yield, event wait/wakeup, timed sleep, and context-switch tests. The OVMF thread smoke passed these paths.
- [x] Add single-vCPU PIT timer-driven preemption after locking, stack, timer, wait-queue, and interrupt-return invariants have deterministic tests. The OVMF `thread-smoke` verifies two non-yielding workers both run, checks x87/SSE state survives asynchronous preemption, and validates the IRQ-save lock's IF behavior. Timer EOI is issued before a context switch; IRQ/exception handlers remain bounded and allocation-free. SMP remains a separate later sub-milestone.
- [x] Implement interrupt-driven UART RX and PS/2 raw-scancode queues with bounded buffers and scheduler event wakeups; preserve polling fallback. OVMF `input-smoke` sends a shell command over UART and verifies a PS/2 make scancode after the shell blocks for input.

**Exit criteria:** met locally for the single-vCPU scope. `just verify` passed on 2026-11-13, covering host tests, target check/build, BIOS/OVMF boot, APIC routing/PIT EOI, active mapping/TLB behavior, guarded stacks, cooperative waits, non-yielding timer preemption, FPU-state preservation, IRQ-save lock IF restoration, and UART/PS/2 wakeups. IRQ/exception handlers remain allocation-free. SMP, physical-hardware validation, and userspace are still out of scope.
