    #[test]
    fn rejects_user_entries_at_every_kernel_table_level() {
        let root = parse_cr3_root(0x1000, Some(40), false).unwrap();

        let mut root_user = SyntheticReader::new();
        root_user.set(0x1000, 256, 0x2007);
        assert_eq!(
            validate_supervisor_kernel_half(&root_user, root, four_level_walk_config()),
            Err(KernelHalfValidationError::UserAccessibleEntry {
                level: 4,
                index: 256,
            })
        );

        let mut intermediate_user = SyntheticReader::new();
        intermediate_user.set(0x1000, 256, 0x2003);
        intermediate_user.set(0x2000, 0, 0x3007);
        assert_eq!(
            validate_supervisor_kernel_half(&intermediate_user, root, four_level_walk_config()),
            Err(KernelHalfValidationError::UserAccessibleEntry { level: 3, index: 0 })
        );

        let mut leaf_user = SyntheticReader::new();
        leaf_user.set(0x1000, 256, 0x2003);
        leaf_user.set(0x2000, 0, 0x3003);
        leaf_user.set(0x3000, 0, 0x4003);
        leaf_user.set(0x4000, 0, 0x5007);
        assert_eq!(
            validate_supervisor_kernel_half(&leaf_user, root, four_level_walk_config()),
            Err(KernelHalfValidationError::UserAccessibleEntry { level: 1, index: 0 })
        );

        let mut large_leaf_user = SyntheticReader::new();
        large_leaf_user.set(0x1000, 256, 0x2003);
        large_leaf_user.set(0x2000, 0x0, 0x4000_0087);
        assert_eq!(
            validate_supervisor_kernel_half(&large_leaf_user, root, four_level_walk_config()),
            Err(KernelHalfValidationError::UserAccessibleEntry { level: 3, index: 0 })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_invalid_or_cross_level_aliased_kernel_tables() {
        let root = parse_cr3_root(0x1000, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        let mut invalid_large_root = SyntheticReader::new();
        invalid_large_root.set(0x1000, 256, 0x2083);
        assert_eq!(
            validate_supervisor_kernel_half(&invalid_large_root, root, four_level_walk_config()),
            Err(KernelHalfValidationError::InvalidEntry {
                level: 4,
                index: 256,
            })
        );

        let mut aliased_table = SyntheticReader::new();
        aliased_table.set(0x1000, 256, 0x2003);
        aliased_table.set(0x2000, 0, 0x2003);
        assert_eq!(
            validate_supervisor_kernel_half(&aliased_table, root, four_level_walk_config()),
            Err(KernelHalfValidationError::TableAliasedAcrossLevels {
                physical_address: 0x2000,
                first_level: 3,
                second_level: 2,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn accepts_aligned_ranges_at_canonical_boundaries() {
        let lower = validate_mapping_range(
            0x0000_7fff_ffff_e000,
            0x1000,
            0x2000,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(14),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            lower,
            ValidatedMappingRange {
                virtual_start: 0x0000_7fff_ffff_e000,
                virtual_end: 0x0000_8000_0000_0000,
                physical_start: 0x1000,
                physical_end: 0x3000,
                physical_address_bits: 14,
                permissions: KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            }
        );

        let upper = validate_mapping_range(
            0xffff_8000_0000_0000,
            0,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(12),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(upper.virtual_end(), 0xffff_8000_0000_1000);
    }

    #[test]
    fn user_mappings_are_confined_to_the_lower_canonical_half() {
        let user_read_only = PagePermissions {
            writable: false,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        };

        for (virtual_address_bits, upper_half_start) in [
            (48, 0xffff_8000_0000_0000),
            (57, 0xff00_0000_0000_0000),
            (64, 0x8000_0000_0000_0000),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(
                validate_mapping_range(
                    upper_half_start,
                    0x1000,
                    PAGE_SIZE,
                    user_read_only,
                    Some(40),
                    virtual_address_bits,
                ),
                Err(MappingError::UserMappingOutsideLowerHalf)
            );

            let lower_half_last_page = (1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1)) - PAGE_SIZE;
            assert!(validate_mapping_range(
                lower_half_last_page,
                0x1000,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                user_read_only,
                Some(40),
                virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .is_ok());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_empty_and_unaligned_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x2000, 0, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(32), 48),
            Err(MappingError::EmptyRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1001, 0x2000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(32), 48),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                0x2000,
                PAGE_SIZE + 1,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(32),
                48
            ),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedRange)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn requires_known_valid_address_widths_and_bounded_physical_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, None, 48),
            Err(MappingError::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(0), 48),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(52), 0),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                0x1000,
                PAGE_SIZE * 2,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(13),
                48
            ),
            Err(MappingError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_noncanonical_ranges_and_ranges_crossing_the_canonical_hole() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x0000_8000_0000_0000,
                0,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(52),
                48
            ),
            Err(MappingError::NonCanonicalVirtualRange)
        );

        let crosses_hole = (0xffff_8000_0000_1000u64) - 0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000;
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000,
                0,
                crosses_hole,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                48,
            ),
            Err(MappingError::CrossesCanonicalHole)
        );
    }

    fn pat_value(entries: [u8; 8]) -> u64 {
        entries.iter().enumerate().fold(0, |value, (index, entry)| {
            value | ((*entry as u64) << (index * 8))
        })
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolves_cache_policies_from_the_supplied_pat_layout() {
        let pat = pat_value([6, 4, 7, 0, 6, 1, 7, 0]);
        let layout = super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(layout.index_for(super::CachePolicy::WriteBack), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(layout.index_for(super::CachePolicy::Uncacheable), Some(3));
        assert_eq!(
            layout.index_for(super::CachePolicy::WriteCombining),
            Some(5)
        );

        let without_write_combining =
            super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 4, 7, 0, 6, 4, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            without_write_combining.index_for(super::CachePolicy::WriteCombining),
            None
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn combines_every_documented_pat_and_mtrr_pair() {
        use EffectiveMemoryType as E;
        use MtrrMemoryType as M;

        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([0, 7, 1, 4, 6, 5, 0, 0])).unwrap();
        let rows = [
            (
                M::Uncacheable,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteCombining,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteThrough,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteBack,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteBack,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteProtected,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                ],
            ),
        ];

        for (mtrr_type, expected) in rows {
            let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(1 << 10, (1 << 11) | mtrr_type as u64);
            let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
            for (pat_index, expected_type) in expected.into_iter().enumerate() {
                assert_eq!(
                    layout.effective_memory_type_for(0x20_0000, pat, pat_index as u8, true),
                    Ok(expected_type),
                    "MTRR={mtrr_type:?}, PAT index={pat_index}"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_invalid_effective_cache_type_inputs() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 4, 7, 0, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.effective_memory_type_for(0, pat, 8, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::PatIndexOutOfRange { index: 8 })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.effective_memory_type_for(0, pat, 0, false),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::NonNormalCachingMode)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.effective_memory_type_for(1u64 << 36, pat, 0, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::Mtrr(
                MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange
            ))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn selects_a_pat_index_that_is_uniform_across_variable_mtrr_segments() {
        let capability = 1 | (1 << 10);
        let mut registers =
            empty_mtrr_registers(capability, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        registers.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: 0x20_0000 | MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask & !(0x20_0000 - 1)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(
                0x1f_f000,
                PAGE_SIZE * 2,
                pat,
                EffectiveMemoryType::WriteCombining,
                true,
            ),
            Ok(2)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_range_when_fixed_mtrrs_prevent_one_uniform_pat_index() {
        let mut registers = empty_mtrr_registers(
            1 << 8,
            (1 << 11) | (1 << 10) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
        );
        registers.fixed_registers.as_mut().unwrap()[0] = MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64;
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(
                0,
                0x20_000,
                pat,
                EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack,
                true,
            ),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::NoUniformPatIndex {
                requested: EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_invalid_effective_cache_type_ranges() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        let requested = EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack;

        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(0, 0, pat, requested, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::EmptyRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(1, PAGE_SIZE, pat, requested, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::UnalignedRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(
                u64::MAX & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                pat,
                requested,
                true,
            ),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(1 << 36, PAGE_SIZE, pat, requested, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::Mtrr(
                MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange
            ))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(0, PAGE_SIZE, pat, requested, false),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::NonNormalCachingMode)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_captured_mtrr_snapshot_before_resolution() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(
            (1 << 12) | (1 << 10) | (1 << 8) | 1,
            (1 << 11) | (1 << 10) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
        );
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(layout.memory_type_for(0), Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack));
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x10_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.capability |= 1 << 9;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedCapabilityBits)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.capability |= 1 << 13;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedCapabilityBits)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.default_type |= 1 << 12;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedDefaultTypeBits)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.variable_register_count = 1;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::VariableRegisterCountMismatch)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1 << 8, 1 << 11);
        invalid.fixed_registers = None;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::FixedRegisterSupportMismatch)
        );

        let invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining as u64);
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1 << 8, (1 << 11) | 6);
        invalid.fixed_registers.as_mut().unwrap()[0] =
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining as u64 * 0x0101_0101_0101_0101;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1, (1 << 11) | 6);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        invalid.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: 0x20_0000 | MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask & !(0x20_0000 - 1)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported)
        );

        let invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | (1 << 10));
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::FixedRangesUnavailable)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1, 1 << 11);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        invalid.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask ^ (1 << 13)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::UnsupportedDiscontinuousVariableMask)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_misaligned_variable_mtrr_bases() {
        let physical_address_bits = 36;
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        let mask = physical_mask & !(0x2000 - 1) | (1 << 11);
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(
                0x1000 | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
                mask,
                physical_address_bits,
            ),
            Err(MtrrError::MisalignedVariableBase)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_reserved_pat_entries() {
        assert_eq!(
            super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x08),
            Err(super::PatLayoutError::ReservedBits { index: 0 })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(0b010 << 24),
            Err(super::PatLayoutError::ReservedMemoryType {
                index: 3,
                value: 0b010,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn selects_uniform_cache_attributes_for_a_mapping_range_and_encodes_each_leaf() {
        let capability = 1 | (1 << 10);
        let mut registers =
            empty_mtrr_registers(capability, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        registers.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: 0x20_0000 | MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask & !(0x20_0000 - 1)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        let mtrrs = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0x4000,
            0x1f_f000,
            PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(36),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let attributes = mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteCombining, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(attributes.physical_start(), 0x1f_f000);
        assert_eq!(attributes.physical_end(), 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(attributes.pat_index(), 2);
        assert_eq!(
            attributes.effective_type(),
            EffectiveMemoryType::WriteCombining
        );
        for offset in [0, PAGE_SIZE] {
            assert_eq!(
                mapping
                    .leaf_4k_entry_with_cache_attributes(offset, attributes, true)
                    .unwrap()
                    .bits()
                    & ((1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7)),
                1 << 4
            );
        }

        let other_mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0x8000,
            0x30_0000,
            PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(36),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            other_mapping.leaf_4k_entry_with_cache_attributes(0, attributes, true),
            Err(MappingError::CacheAttributesRangeMismatch)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_cache_attribute_selection_when_physical_widths_disagree() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let mtrrs = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        let mapping =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(37), 48)
                .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            mapping.select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true),
            Err(MappingError::MtrrPhysicalAddressWidthMismatch)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn encodes_4k_leaf_permissions_nx_and_pat_index_bits() {
        let writable_user_page = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        };
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0x4000,
            0x20_0000,
            PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            writable_user_page,
            Some(52),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();

        let first = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0b101, true).unwrap().bits();
        assert_eq!(
            first,
            0x20_0000 | (1 << 0) | (1 << 1) | (1 << 2) | (1 << 3) | (1 << 7) | (1 << 63)
        );
        let second = mapping
            .leaf_4k_entry(PAGE_SIZE, 0b101, true)
            .unwrap()
            .bits();
        assert_eq!(second & 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000, 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(second & (1 << 63), 1 << 63);

        let all_pat_bits = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0b111, true).unwrap().bits()
            & ((1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7));
        assert_eq!(all_pat_bits, (1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_unencodable_leaf_attributes_and_page_offsets() {
        let mapping =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(52), 48)
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 8, true),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPatIndex)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, false),
            Err(MappingError::NxNotEnabled)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(1, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedPageOffset)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(PAGE_SIZE, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::PageOffsetOutOfRange)
        );

        let too_wide =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(53), 48)
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            too_wide.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn executable_leaf_does_not_set_nx() {
        let executable = PagePermissions {
            writable: false,
            executable: true,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mapping =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, executable, Some(52), 48).unwrap();
        let entry = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, false).unwrap().bits();
        assert_eq!(entry, 0x20_0000 | 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_reject_root_frames_outside_the_configured_width() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: high_address,
            length: PAGE_SIZE,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let failure =
            match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config()) {
                Err(error) => error,
                Ok(_) => panic!("candidate creation accepted an out-of-range root frame"),
            };
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateCreateErrorKind::RootFrameOutOfRange);
        let frame = failure
            .frame
            .expect("root token is returned on validation failure");
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), high_address);
        allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_mapping_rejects_out_of_width_table_frames_transactionally() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_1000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: high_address,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), 0x10_1000);
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            0xffff_9000_0000_1000,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::TableFrameOutOfRange);
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_walk_rejects_intermediate_tables_without_owned_tokens() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(2);

        let candidate =

    #[test]
    fn candidate_release_failure_retains_owned_frames_for_retry() {
        const TOTAL_FRAMES: usize = 513;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(TOTAL_FRAMES);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let mut remaining_frames: [Option<Frame>; TOTAL_FRAMES - 1] =
            core::array::from_fn(|_| Some(allocator.allocate().unwrap()));
        for index in (1..remaining_frames.len()).step_by(2) {
            allocator
                .deallocate(remaining_frames[index].take().unwrap())
                .unwrap();
        }

        let failure = match candidate.release(&mut allocator) {
            Err(failure) => failure,
            Ok(()) => panic!("release unexpectedly fit a full range table"),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            failure.error,
            CandidateReleaseError::Frame(FrameError::RangeTableFull)
        );
        assert_eq!(failure.candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(failure.candidate.mapping_count(), 0);

        allocator
            .deallocate(remaining_frames[0].take().unwrap())
            .unwrap();
        failure.candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        for frame in remaining_frames.into_iter().flatten() {
            allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), TOTAL_FRAMES as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn active_candidate_rejects_mutation_and_release_until_deactivated() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(4);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
        // SAFETY: This is a synthetic test of the active-state guard; no CPU
        // actually uses the test candidate's root.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        assert!(candidate.is_active());
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(0xffff_9000_0000_1000),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::Active)
        ));

        let failure = candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.error, CandidateReleaseError::ActiveRoot);
        let mut candidate = failure.candidate;
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), root);
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test never installed this root in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn active_owned_mapping_invalidates_before_returning_frame_ownership() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(8);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical_address = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: true,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        candidate.memory.record_events = true;
        // SAFETY: The host backend records invalidations and no hardware CR3 is
        // changed; this tests active API state and ownership ordering only.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        // SAFETY: Synthetic active-root ownership is established above, and the
        // backend's invalidation operation records this leaf address.
        unsafe {
            candidate
                .map_owned_page_active(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
                .unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidation_count, 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidated_pages[0], virtual_address);
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[3],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::PageWrite { value, .. }) if value & 1 != 0
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[4],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::Invalidate { virtual_address })
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address),
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                if translation.physical_address == physical_address
        ));

        // SAFETY: The synthetic root remains the candidate's current test root;
        // unmap invalidates the address before the frame token is returned.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidation_count, 2);
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidated_pages[1], virtual_address);
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[5],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::PageWrite { value: 0, .. })
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[6],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::Invalidate { virtual_address })
        );
        allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        // SAFETY: No real CPU installed this host-test candidate in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_clone_preserves_inherited_entries_and_shared_tables() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let indexes = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4);
        let source_root = 0x8000;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0], 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0] + 1, 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0x9000, indexes[1], 0xa000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xa000, indexes[2], 0xb000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xb000, indexes[3], 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 63));

        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        candidate
            .clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: 0x20_0000,
                leaf_physical_base: 0x20_0000,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: PagePermissions {
                    writable: true,
                    executable: false,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 63),
            })
        );

        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn inherited_large_page_permission_change_splits_and_preserves_cache_type() {
        let total_frames = 16;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let indexes = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4);
        let source_root = 0x8000;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0], 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0x9000, indexes[1], 0xa000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xa000, indexes[2], 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 7) | (1 << 12));
        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        candidate
            .clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root)
            .unwrap();

        candidate
            .set_inherited_page_permissions(
                &mut allocator,
                virtual_address,
                0x20_1000,
                PagePermissions {
                    writable: false,
                    executable: false,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
            )
            .unwrap();
        let protected = match candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("split mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(protected.physical_address, 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(protected.page_size, PAGE_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(
            protected.permissions,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(protected.pat_index, 4);

        let neighbor = match candidate.walk(virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("neighbor mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(neighbor.physical_address, 0x20_2000);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.page_size, PAGE_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.permissions.writable, true);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.permissions.executable, true);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.pat_index, 4);

        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

        let error = match invalid {

    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_borrowed_acpi_without_owning_its_frame() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let acpi_physical = 0x20_0000;
        let acpi_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: acpi_physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = acpi_map
            .validate_acpi_span(acpi_physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            acpi_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map - 3);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: acpi_physical,
                leaf_physical_base: acpi_physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: acpi_physical | 1 | (1 << 63),
            })
        );
        let duplicate_virtual = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            duplicate_virtual.cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::MappingAlreadyPresent
        );
        let other_virtual = virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE;
        let other_mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            other_virtual,
            acpi_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let duplicate_physical = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, other_mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            duplicate_physical.cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::PhysicalPageAlreadyMapped
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::OwnershipMismatch)
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        // SAFETY: This synthetic test checks the inactive-only guard; the CPU
        // never installs the candidate's root.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_acpi_page(virtual_address),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::Active)
        );
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test never installed this root in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.unmap_acpi_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_explicit_uncacheable_mmio_without_frame_ownership() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let mmio_physical = 0xfee0_0000;
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_d000_0000_0000;
        let mmio_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: 0x10_0000,
            length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mmio_span = mmio_map
            .validate_mmio_page(mmio_physical, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            mmio_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            permissions,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let attributes = super::SelectedCacheAttributes {
            physical_start: mmio_physical,
            physical_end: mmio_physical + PAGE_SIZE,
            pat_index: 3,
            effective_type: EffectiveMemoryType::Uncacheable,
        };
        let before = allocator.free_frames();
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test treats this as a device page and never
        // dereferences it; the API's map authorization, range, permissions, and
        // UC requirements apply.
        unsafe {
            candidate
                .map_mmio_page(&mut allocator, mmio_span, mapping, attributes)
                .unwrap()
        };
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), before - 3);
        let translation = match candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("MMIO mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(translation.physical_address, mmio_physical);
        assert_eq!(translation.permissions, permissions);
        assert_eq!(translation.pat_index, 3);
        assert_eq!(translation.raw_leaf_entry & (1 << 63), 1 << 63);

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_mmio_page(virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::NotMapped)
        );
        candidate.unmap_mmio_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

        .unwrap();

        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = writable
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let failure = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, writable, attributes)

                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, executable, executable_attributes)

            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, wrong_span, read_only, read_only_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn borrowed_acpi_mapping_rolls_back_new_tables_on_frame_exhaustion() {
        let total_frames = 3;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let physical = 0x20_0000;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = map
            .validate_acpi_span(physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0xffff_9000_0000_1000,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::OutOfFrames);
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_unmap_and_release_owned_frames() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), Some(root));
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0x0000_4000_0000_1000;
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        };
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(&frame, virtual_address, permissions);

        candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: physical,
                leaf_physical_base: physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: physical | 0x3 | (1 << 2) | (1 << 63),
            })
        );

        let duplicate_frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let (duplicate_mapping, duplicate_attributes) =
            candidate_mapping(&duplicate_frame, virtual_address, permissions);
        let free_before_duplicate = allocator.free_frames();
        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(
                &mut allocator,
                duplicate_frame,
                duplicate_mapping,
                duplicate_attributes,
            )
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::MappingAlreadyPresent);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_duplicate);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();

        let returned = candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(returned.address(), physical);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent {
                level: PageLevel::Pt,
            }
        );
        allocator.deallocate(returned).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_table_mapping_rolls_back_on_frame_exhaustion() {
        let total_frames = 4;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::OutOfFrames);
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_table_mapping_rolls_back_after_prepare_failure() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        memory.fail_prepare_at = Some(3);
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            failure.cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::TableMemory(CandidateTestMemoryError::InjectedPrepareFailure)
        );
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_support_five_level_virtual_paths() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let config = PageWalkConfig {
            levels: 5,
            virtual_address_bits: 57,
            ..four_level_walk_config()
        };
        let mut candidate = CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, config).unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), Some(root));
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0xff00_0000_0020_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: true,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );

        candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 5);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: physical,
                leaf_physical_base: physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: PagePermissions {
                    writable: false,
                    executable: true,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: physical | 0x1,
            })
        );
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_arithmetic_overflow_and_writable_executable_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                0,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );

        let writable_executable = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: true,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x2000, PAGE_SIZE, writable_executable, Some(52), 48),
            Err(MappingError::WritableExecutable)
        );
    }
}

```rustix/docs/architecture/syscall-abi.md
     1	# Unix-like process and syscall direction
     2	
     3	**Status: design direction only. No process, syscall, or userland support is implemented.**
     4	
     5	Rustix aims to expose a small, versioned syscall surface that can support Unix-like processes and tools. The kernel must own this interface rather than inherit an ABI accidentally from a bootloader or emulator.
     6	
     7	## Proposed compatibility principles
     8	
     9	- Processes have independent virtual address spaces and explicit lifecycle states.
    10	- File descriptors are per-process integer handles to kernel-managed objects; descriptor inheritance, close-on-exec, duplication, and sharing semantics must be specified together.
    11	- Syscalls use one documented error convention and stable numeric identifiers. New operations must not silently repurpose old numbers.
    12	- Arguments crossing privilege boundaries are copied or validated using narrowly scoped helpers. User memory is never dereferenced as a trusted Rust reference.
    13	- Blocking, interruption, cancellation, and restart behavior are explicit for each syscall class.
    14	- A compatibility layer (for example, POSIX-shaped libc behavior) remains separate from internal kernel APIs.
    15	
    16	## Initial x86_64 entry design (Milestone 4; not implemented)
    17	
    18	The first single-vCPU user-mode slice will enter the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated IDT interrupt gate at DPL 3 and return with `IRETQ`. This intentionally avoids `SYSCALL`/`SYSRET`, `STAR`/`LSTAR`/`FMASK`, and `SWAPGS` state transitions in the first userspace path. It is a provisional architecture decision, not a published or implemented syscall ABI.
    19	
    20	- **Vector ownership:** `0x80` is currently inside Rustix's device-vector allocation range (`0x20..=0xef`). Before installing the user-callable gate, reserve it from `InterruptVectorAllocator` and install a dedicated syscall stub rather than the generic device-IRQ stub. The gate must be an interrupt gate, so maskable interrupts are disabled on entry before Rust dispatch.
    21	- **Selectors:** the current GDT uses `0x08` for kernel code, `0x10` for kernel data, and `0x18` for the two-slot TSS descriptor. Append ring-3 data and code descriptors after the TSS without moving existing selectors: user data selector `0x2b` and user code selector `0x33` (GDT indexes 5 and 6 with RPL 3). The user code descriptor must be 64-bit code; the data selector is loaded into user `SS` on return. These values are a design target and must be asserted by the GDT implementation/tests before use.
    22	- **Privilege stack:** a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt uses `TSS.RSP0`; it must point to the top of the current process's mapped, writable kernel-entry stack before user execution is resumed. The existing TSS points to one static bootstrap ring-0 stack, so it is not sufficient for processes. On this single-vCPU design the scheduler must update `RSP0` whenever it selects a process to run in user mode. A future SMP design needs per-CPU TSS and entry-stack state.
    23	- **Entry frame and state:** the assembly stub must preserve the complete user register state and construct a separately specified syscall frame; it must not assume the existing fatal-exception frame is interchangeable. Kernel code must run with the direction flag clear. Preserve user x87/SSE state across kernel handling; AVX remains disabled under the current CPU-state policy. Do not form Rust references from user pointers.
    24	- **Initial register convention:** `RAX` carries the syscall number; arguments use `RDI`, `RSI`, `RDX`, `R10`, `R8`, and `R9`; `RAX` carries the result. This is only a proposed register convention. It becomes stable only together with ABI version discovery, syscall numbers, errors, and transfer semantics below.
    25	- **Return validation:** use `IRETQ`, not `SYSRET`. Before returning, validate that the saved `CS` and `SS` are exactly the ring-3 selectors, `RIP` and `RSP` are canonical and within the process's executable/code and stack regions respectively, and `RFLAGS` contains no privileged or unsupported bits. Construct a safe flags value rather than echoing user-controlled flags. A malformed frame terminates the process with a reported status; never attempt the return and rely on a ring-0 `#GP` to catch it.
    26	- **NMI and interrupt policy:** no GS-base swap is needed on this entry path. An NMI can still arrive during entry; the current NMI/exception path is fatal-only, and this design does not claim to recover from it. Keep that behavior explicit until user-origin exception/NMI policy is implemented and tested. Ordinary maskable IRQs may resume only after the entry state and scheduler ownership are consistent.
    27	
    28	This design depends on a process-owned address space that maps the syscall entry/return code, IDT, GDT, TSS, and the active kernel stack safely. No Ring 3 execution should be enabled until the address-space implementation is reviewed and validated.
    29	
    30	### Process address spaces (design; not implemented)
    31	
    32	Use a separate four- or five-level root per process. Each process root owns its root page, all lower-half intermediate tables, and every user leaf frame. Keep the current kernel address-space owner alive for the lifetime of every process root. Copy only upper-half top-level entries from that owner into each process root; these entries are non-owning references to shared kernel subtrees, not deep copies, and must never be released by a process teardown. Do not copy lower-half entries from the kernel root.
    33	
    34	Before publishing a shared kernel subtree, validate its page-table structure and physical bounds and reject any present entry with the user/supervisor bit set at any level. Shared kernel mappings therefore remain supervisor-only regardless of the process-owned user mappings. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.
    35	
    36	The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. Before releasing a process root or any of its user frames, switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate the local non-global translations; keep the shared kernel owner alive. Do not add PCID or SMP teardown/shootdown behavior implicitly: those require a separate design.
    37	
    38	The current `CandidatePageTables` deep-clones the inherited hierarchy, tracks all cloned table frames as owned, holds an exclusive mutable borrow of one memory backend, and does not provide shared-subtree ownership. It is not itself the process-address-space abstraction. Implement the shared-root policy in a distinct owner/handle API that can safely support multiple process roots without aliasing mutable backend references. Until that implementation and its negative tests exist, these paragraphs are a design contract only.
    39	
    40	## ABI decisions still required before exposing calls
    41	
    42	1. ABI version discovery and compatibility guarantees.
    43	2. Error encoding and a complete initial syscall-number allocation.
    44	3. Pointer/length validation, partial reads/writes, and copy-fault behavior.
    45	4. Process creation and execution semantics, including file actions and inherited descriptors.
    46	5. Signal-like asynchronous delivery, interruption, and restart semantics.
    47	6. Time, clocks, and structure layout rules.
    48	
    49	## Suggested first user-visible slice
    50	
    51	After address spaces, scheduler, and storage primitives exist, implement a controlled `init` process with a small syscall subset: process exit, read/write through descriptors, open/close, and wait. Add end-to-end tests for invalid pointers, partial transfers, descriptor lifetime, process exit status, and ABI version negotiation before describing it as Unix-compatible.

```

   172	## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI
   173	
   174	Userspace begins only after page tables, exception handling, scheduling, and controlled memory allocation are trustworthy. The syscall ABI is a product interface and must not emerge accidentally from internal functions. Milestone 3's single-vCPU IRQ-safe locking and timer-preemption gate is locally validated; this enables scheduler progress but does not by itself make user code isolated or safe. SMP remains outside this milestone.
   175	
   176	### Planned work
   177	
   178	- [x] Decide and document the initial x86_64 user-entry/syscall mechanism, register convention, selector/MSR setup, per-CPU state requirements, and safe return path. The current design proposes a DPL-3 `int $0x80` gate and validated `IRETQ` return, with no syscall MSRs or `SWAPGS`; implementation and validation remain pending. Revisit the choice if the entry model or SMP requirements change.
   179	- [x] Define per-process address-space construction without deep-cloning the entire kernel page-table tree for every process. The design shares validated supervisor-only upper-half subtrees, keeps lower-half tables and user frames process-owned, and specifies kernel-owner lifetime, teardown, permission, and local TLB rules. Implementation and validation remain pending.
   180	- [ ] Add user/kernel page permissions and process-owned address spaces, including teardown and TLB invalidation rules.
   181	- [ ] Implement copy-in/copy-out helpers that validate lengths, arithmetic, canonical ranges, permissions, and faults; never form a kernel reference directly from a user pointer.
   182	- [ ] Specify version discovery, stable syscall numbers, argument layouts, error encoding, partial-I/O behavior, interruption/restart, and compatibility policy before exposing calls.
   183	- [ ] Add initial process lifecycle and descriptor-table semantics: create/load, exit, wait, close, duplication/inheritance, and process cleanup.
   184	- [ ] Load statically linked ELF64 executables with checked `PT_LOAD` bounds, alignment, permissions, and entry points; reject malformed binaries safely. Use `.bin` for command-line programs and `.app` for GUI applications as role-based filename suffixes for the same underlying format. `.app` is a Rustix single-file application suffix, not an Apple/macOS app bundle; initially require application resources to be embedded or absent.
   185	- [ ] Add user-mode exception handling: faults attributable to Ring 3 terminate the offending process with a reported status, while faults in kernel mode remain fatal. Test page faults, general-protection faults, invalid opcodes, and divide errors from both privilege levels.
   186	- [ ] Define user virtual-memory regions, stack bounds/guard behavior, and a minimal anonymous allocation interface such as `mmap`/`munmap` (or a documented equivalent) before running general user programs. Add bounds, permissions, exhaustion, and teardown tests.
   187	- [ ] Add a small, `no_std`-friendly shared userspace runtime crate (for example, `librustix`) for process entry, syscall wrappers, panic handling, common I/O/formatting, and a user allocator backed by the anonymous mapping interface. Keep it separate from kernel internals and use it from independent application crates; initial executables remain statically linked ELF64 binaries, with application resources embedded or absent.
   188	- [ ] Keep the first user-visible target as a minimal `init` executable loaded from a bounded boot payload or other reproducible non-filesystem source; persistent filesystem loading and ordinary command utilities follow in Milestones 5 and 6.
   189	- [ ] Build adversarial tests for bad pointers, overflow, invalid mappings, user/kernel fault separation, process teardown, descriptor misuse, and failed exec.
   190	
   191	### First user-visible target
   192	
   193	A small controlled `init` process should start from a reproducible image, write through a descriptor, exit with a status, and be waited on by a kernel test harness. Do not claim userspace or process isolation from ring-0 tasks that merely use process-shaped structs.
   194	
   195	**Exit criteria:** an isolated init process runs in user mode and uses a versioned, documented syscall subset; invalid user pointers and process teardown are tested without corrupting the kernel.

# Unix-like process and syscall direction

**Status: design direction only. No process, syscall, or userland support is implemented.**

Rustix aims to expose a small, versioned syscall surface that can support Unix-like processes and tools. The kernel must own this interface rather than inherit an ABI accidentally from a bootloader or emulator.

## Proposed compatibility principles

- Processes have independent virtual address spaces and explicit lifecycle states.
- File descriptors are per-process integer handles to kernel-managed objects; descriptor inheritance, close-on-exec, duplication, and sharing semantics must be specified together.
- Syscalls use one documented error convention and stable numeric identifiers. New operations must not silently repurpose old numbers.
- Arguments crossing privilege boundaries are copied or validated using narrowly scoped helpers. User memory is never dereferenced as a trusted Rust reference.
- Blocking, interruption, cancellation, and restart behavior are explicit for each syscall class.
- A compatibility layer (for example, POSIX-shaped libc behavior) remains separate from internal kernel APIs.

## Initial x86_64 entry design (Milestone 4; not implemented)

The first single-vCPU user-mode slice will enter the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated IDT interrupt gate at DPL 3 and return with `IRETQ`. This intentionally avoids `SYSCALL`/`SYSRET`, `STAR`/`LSTAR`/`FMASK`, and `SWAPGS` state transitions in the first userspace path. It is a provisional architecture decision, not a published or implemented syscall ABI.

- **Vector ownership:** `0x80` is currently inside Rustix's device-vector allocation range (`0x20..=0xef`). Before installing the user-callable gate, reserve it from `InterruptVectorAllocator` and install a dedicated syscall stub rather than the generic device-IRQ stub. The gate must be an interrupt gate, so maskable interrupts are disabled on entry before Rust dispatch.
- **Selectors:** the current GDT uses `0x08` for kernel code, `0x10` for kernel data, and `0x18` for the two-slot TSS descriptor. Append ring-3 data and code descriptors after the TSS without moving existing selectors: user data selector `0x2b` and user code selector `0x33` (GDT indexes 5 and 6 with RPL 3). The user code descriptor must be 64-bit code; the data selector is loaded into user `SS` on return. These values are a design target and must be asserted by the GDT implementation/tests before use.
- **Privilege stack:** a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt uses `TSS.RSP0`; it must point to the top of the current process's mapped, writable kernel-entry stack before user execution is resumed. The existing TSS points to one static bootstrap ring-0 stack, so it is not sufficient for processes. On this single-vCPU design the scheduler must update `RSP0` whenever it selects a process to run in user mode. A future SMP design needs per-CPU TSS and entry-stack state.
- **Entry frame and state:** the assembly stub must preserve the complete user register state and construct a separately specified syscall frame; it must not assume the existing fatal-exception frame is interchangeable. Kernel code must run with the direction flag clear. Preserve user x87/SSE state across kernel handling; AVX remains disabled under the current CPU-state policy. Do not form Rust references from user pointers.
- **Initial register convention:** `RAX` carries the syscall number; arguments use `RDI`, `RSI`, `RDX`, `R10`, `R8`, and `R9`; `RAX` carries the result. This is only a proposed register convention. It becomes stable only together with ABI version discovery, syscall numbers, errors, and transfer semantics below.
- **Return validation:** use `IRETQ`, not `SYSRET`. Before returning, validate that the saved `CS` and `SS` are exactly the ring-3 selectors, `RIP` and `RSP` are canonical and within the process's executable/code and stack regions respectively, and `RFLAGS` contains no privileged or unsupported bits. Construct a safe flags value rather than echoing user-controlled flags. A malformed frame terminates the process with a reported status; never attempt the return and rely on a ring-0 `#GP` to catch it.
- **NMI and interrupt policy:** no GS-base swap is needed on this entry path. An NMI can still arrive during entry; the current NMI/exception path is fatal-only, and this design does not claim to recover from it. Keep that behavior explicit until user-origin exception/NMI policy is implemented and tested. Ordinary maskable IRQs may resume only after the entry state and scheduler ownership are consistent.

This design depends on a process-owned address space that maps the syscall entry/return code, IDT, GDT, TSS, and the active kernel stack safely. No Ring 3 execution should be enabled until the address-space implementation is reviewed and validated.

### Process address spaces (design; not implemented)

Use a separate four- or five-level root per process. The initial source is the retained active clone of Limine's hierarchy, not a curated clean-room root. Each process root owns its root page, all lower-half intermediate tables, and every user leaf frame. Keep the kernel-root owner alive for the lifetime of every process root. Copy only upper-half top-level entries from that owner into each process root; these entries are non-owning references to shared kernel subtrees, not deep copies, and must never be released by a process teardown. Do not copy lower-half entries from the kernel root.

Before publishing a shared kernel subtree, validate its page-table structure and physical bounds and reject any present entry with the user/supervisor bit set at any level. `paging::validate_supervisor_kernel_half` implements this bounded preflight, but it does not install roots or prove physical backing is readable; the supplied reader must provide that access guarantee. Sharing the active clone means every accepted upper-half supervisor mapping and alias is present in every process CR3. This is not a curated kernel map or kernel-page-table isolation, and it provides no transient-execution protection. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.

The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. Before releasing a process root or any of its user frames, switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate the local non-global translations; keep the shared kernel owner alive. Do not add PCID or SMP teardown/shootdown behavior implicitly: those require a separate design.

The current `CandidatePageTables` deep-clones the inherited hierarchy, tracks all cloned table frames as owned, holds an exclusive mutable borrow of one memory backend, and does not provide shared-subtree ownership. It is not itself the process-address-space abstraction. Implement the shared-root policy in a distinct owner/handle API that can safely support multiple process roots without aliasing mutable backend references. Until that implementation and its negative tests exist, these paragraphs are a design contract only.

## ABI decisions still required before exposing calls

1. ABI version discovery and compatibility guarantees.
2. Error encoding and a complete initial syscall-number allocation.
3. Pointer/length validation, partial reads/writes, and copy-fault behavior.
4. Process creation and execution semantics, including file actions and inherited descriptors.
5. Signal-like asynchronous delivery, interruption, and restart semantics.
6. Time, clocks, and structure layout rules.

## Suggested first user-visible slice

After address spaces, scheduler, and storage primitives exist, implement a controlled `init` process with a small syscall subset: process exit, read/write through descriptors, open/close, and wait. Add end-to-end tests for invalid pointers, partial transfers, descriptor lifetime, process exit status, and ABI version negotiation before describing it as Unix-compatible.

```
