        match Layout::from_size_align(KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_MAX_PAGES * PAGE_SIZE as usize + 1, 1) {
            Ok(layout) => layout,
            Err(_) => halt_forever(),
        };
    // SAFETY: The request is larger than either bounded arena and must fail.
    let exhausted = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(oversized_layout) };
    if !exhausted.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: Both pointers are live allocations with their original layouts.
        unsafe {
            KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(exhausted, oversized_layout);
            KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(full_arena, full_layout);
        }
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: bounded growth exhaustion was not deterministic");
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: `full_arena` is the complete live allocation created above.
    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(full_arena, full_layout) };

    let layout = match Layout::from_size_align(257, 64) {
        Ok(layout) => layout,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "kernel heap probe failed to construct aligned layout: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    // SAFETY: The heap is available after releasing the full-arena allocation.
    let allocation = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(layout) };
    if allocation.is_null() || allocation as usize % layout.align() != 0 {
        if !allocation.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: This is the live allocation returned for `layout`.
            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(allocation, layout) };
        }
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: aligned allocation was rejected or misaligned");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let Some(allocation) = core::ptr::NonNull::new(allocation) else {
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: aligned allocation was unexpectedly null");
        halt_forever();
    };
    // SAFETY: The allocator returned `layout.size()` writable bytes.
    unsafe { core::ptr::write_bytes(allocation.as_ptr(), 0xa5, layout.size()) };
    for index in 0..layout.size() {
        // SAFETY: `index` remains inside the live allocation.
        if unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().add(index).read_volatile() } != 0xa5 {
            // SAFETY: The allocation is still live with its original layout.
            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(allocation.as_ptr(), layout) };
            kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: allocation data did not round-trip");
            halt_forever();
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: The allocation is live and the original layout is supplied.
    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(allocation.as_ptr(), layout) };
    // SAFETY: The previous allocation was returned; first-fit should reuse it.
    let reused = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(layout) };
    if reused != allocation.as_ptr() {
        if !reused.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: `reused` is a live allocation with `layout`.
            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(reused, layout) };
        }
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: freed space was not reused");
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The reused allocation is live and has the same layout.
    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(reused, layout) };

    let growth_layout = match Layout::from_size_align(
        rustix_kernel::heap::KERNEL_HEAP_CAPACITY + PAGE_SIZE as usize,
        64,
    ) {
        Ok(layout) => layout,
        Err(_) => halt_forever(),
    };
    // SAFETY: This request is larger than the bootstrap arena, so it must use
    // the configured frame-backed range and remain within its fixed limit.
    let growth = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(growth_layout) };
    let Some(growth) = core::ptr::NonNull::new(growth) else {
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: frame-backed allocation was rejected");
        halt_forever();
    };
    let growth_address = growth.as_ptr() as usize;
    let growth_end = KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE as usize
        + KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_MAX_PAGES * PAGE_SIZE as usize;
    if growth_address < KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE as usize
        || growth_address
            .checked_add(growth_layout.size())
            .is_none_or(|end| end > growth_end)
        || growth_address % growth_layout.align() != 0
    {
        // SAFETY: `growth` is the live allocation returned for `growth_layout`.
        unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(growth.as_ptr(), growth_layout) };
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: frame-backed allocation was invalid");
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: GlobalAlloc returned a live allocation, and the checks above keep
    // its complete extent inside the reserved range. The heap mapper commits all
    // pages covering the allocation before returning it. MaybeUninit permits the
    // backing frames to be uninitialized when the mutable view is created.
    let growth_bytes = unsafe {
        core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(
            growth.as_ptr().cast::<core::mem::MaybeUninit<u8>>(),
            growth_layout.size(),
        )
    };
    let last_byte = growth_layout.size() - 1;
    growth_bytes[0].write(0x5a);
    growth_bytes[last_byte].write(0xa5);
    // SAFETY: Both slots were initialized immediately above and are within the
    // validated live allocation. Reading through the references retains the
    // allocation's validity proof for the volatile access.
    let first_byte = unsafe { growth_bytes[0].assume_init_ref() };
    let last_byte = unsafe { growth_bytes[last_byte].assume_init_ref() };
    if unsafe { core::ptr::read_volatile(first_byte) } != 0x5a
        || unsafe { core::ptr::read_volatile(last_byte) } != 0xa5
    {
        // SAFETY: The allocation is still live with its original layout.
        unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(growth.as_ptr(), growth_layout) };
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: frame-backed data did not round-trip");
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: Return the exact growth allocation and then require first-fit reuse.
    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(growth.as_ptr(), growth_layout) };
    let growth_reused = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(growth_layout) };
    if growth_reused != growth.as_ptr() {
        if !growth_reused.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: The pointer is live with `growth_layout`.
            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(growth_reused, growth_layout) };
        }
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: frame-backed space was not reused");
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: Release the reused allocation with its original layout.
    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(growth_reused, growth_layout) };
    kprintln!("kernel heap probe passed: bootstrap exhaustion, frame-backed growth, reuse");
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_hhdm_frame(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE;

    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: no free frame");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let hhdm_address = match frame.hhdm_address(
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe rejected frame translation: {:?}", error);
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let words = (FRAME_SIZE / core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64) as usize;
    let page = hhdm_address as *mut u64;
    let mut verified = true;
    // SAFETY: The non-copyable `Frame` token is held exclusively; its full page
    // is within validated `Usable` memory and its HHDM arithmetic was checked.
    // Limine base revision 3 guarantees usable memory in the HHDM, and no other
    // Rustix mapping aliases this newly allocated frame. This is an opt-in QEMU
    // probe; a broken loader mapping would fault and be caught by the fatal path.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index)
                .write_volatile(0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64);
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            if page.add(index).read_volatile() != (0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64) {
                verified = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index).write_volatile(0);
        }
    }

    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
    if !verified {
        kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: readback mismatch");
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!("HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame");
    probe_inherited_root(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_inherited_root(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address;

    let root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: CR3 decode rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let address = match inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
        root,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: HHDM validation rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let entries = address as *const u64;
    let mut present_entries = 0;
    // SAFETY: The complete root page was validated as bootloader-reclaimable
    // and its HHDM range arithmetic was checked. The Limine base-revision-3
    // contract maps that region; this read-only opt-in probe trusts that handoff.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..512 {
            if entries.add(index).read_volatile() & 1 != 0 {
                present_entries += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    kprintln!(
        "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries, {} present",
        present_entries
    );
    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("inherited page-table walk failed: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "active boot stack",
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
    );

    let pat_value = match boot_info.cpu_info.pat_msr_value {
        Some(value) => value,
        None => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: active PAT value unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let pat = match rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value) {
        Ok(pat) => pat,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid PAT layout: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid MTRR state: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: non-normal CR0 caching mode");
        halt_forever();
    }
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    probe_cloned_page_tables(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        [
            (
                "kernel text",
                segments.text.virtual_start,
                segments.text.physical_start,
                segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel rodata",
                segments.rodata.virtual_start,
                segments.rodata.physical_start,
                segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel data",
                segments.data.virtual_start,
                segments.data.physical_start,
                segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "active boot stack",
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            ),
        ],
    );
    probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_cloned_page_tables(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    spans: [(&str, u64, u64, u64); 4],
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables;

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate = match CandidatePageTables::new(allocator, &mut memory, config) {
        Ok(candidate) => candidate,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                error.cause
            );
            if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                release_probe_frame(allocator, frame);
            }
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(allocator, source_reader, source_root) {
        kprintln!("candidate clone probe failed: {:?}", error);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
    }
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            source_reader,
            source_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed: {} translation mismatch",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
        }
    }
    let table_count = candidate.table_count();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate clone probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate inherited-root clone probe passed: {} owned table pages preserve critical paths; CR3 unchanged",
        table_count
    );
}

fn candidate_span_matches_source(
    candidate: &rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let Some(virtual_address) = virtual_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(expected_physical) = physical_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let source_result =
            walk_virtual_address(source_reader, source_root, virtual_address, config);
        let candidate_result = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
        let (source_translation, candidate_translation) = match (source_result, candidate_result) {
            (Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(source)), Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(candidate))) => {
                (source, candidate)
            }
            (source, candidate) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate clone walk mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}",
                    virtual_address,
                    source,
                    candidate
                );
                return false;
            }
        };
        if !source_translation.same_effective_mapping(candidate_translation)
            || candidate_translation.physical_address != expected_physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone translation mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}, expected PA={:#x}",
                virtual_address,
                source_translation,
                candidate_translation,
                expected_physical
            );
            return false;
        }
        let Some(next_offset) = offset.checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE) else {
            return false;
        };
        offset = next_offset;
    }
    true
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome,
    };

    let Some(physical_address_bits) = boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits else {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: physical width unknown");
        halt_forever();
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled || !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: NXE or normal caching unavailable");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let pat_value = boot_info
        .cpu_info
        .pat_msr_value
        .expect("inherited cache-alias probe validated active PAT");
    let pat = rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value).unwrap_or_else(|error| {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid PAT: {:?}",
            error
        );
        halt_forever();
    });
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid MTRR: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: true,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_ffff_f000;
    let permissions = PagePermissions {
        writable: true,
        executable: false,
        user_accessible: false,
    };
    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: no leaf frame available");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
        virtual_address,
        frame.address(),
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        permissions,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        config.virtual_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(mapping) => mapping,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid mapping: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let cache_attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
        CachePolicy::WriteBack,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
    ) {
        Ok(attributes) => attributes,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: cache policy: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate page-table probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                if let Some(root_frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, root_frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
    let frame_address = frame.address();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.map_owned_page(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        frame,
        mapping,
        cache_attributes,
    ) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to map leaf: {:?}",
            failure.cause
        );
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, failure.frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let walk = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
    let returned_frame = match candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address) {
        Ok(frame) => frame,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed to unmap leaf: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let translation_valid = match &walk {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => {
            translation.physical_address == frame_address
                && translation.page_size == rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE
                && translation.permissions == permissions
                && translation.pat_index == cache_attributes.pat_index()
        }
        _ => false,
    };
    if returned_frame.address() != frame_address {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: unmap returned the wrong frame");
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
    if !translation_valid {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: candidate walk: {:?}",
            walk
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate page-table probe passed: mapped, walked, unmapped, and released root {:#x}; CR3 unchanged",
        root.expect("candidate retains root until release")
    );
}

fn release_candidate_after_probe_failure(
    candidate: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
) -> ! {
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table cleanup also failed: {:?}", failure);
    }
    halt_forever()
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_inherited_mapping(
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    label: &str,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    let mut first_translation: Option<rustix_kernel::paging::PageTranslation> = None;
    let mut permissions_uniform = true;
    let mut pat_index_uniform = true;
    while offset < length {
        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
                if level == rustix_kernel::paging::PageLevel::Pml4 {
                    let pml4_index = ((virtual_address >> 39) & 0x1ff) as u16;
                    let root_entry = reader.read_entry(root.physical_address(), pml4_index);
                    kprintln!(
                        "inherited mapping PML4 detail: VA={:#018x}, index={}, root={:#x}, entry={:?}",
                        virtual_address,
                        pml4_index,
                        root.physical_address(),
                        root_entry
                    );
                }
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
                    label,
                    level
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
                label,
                virtual_address,
                translation.physical_address,
                expected_physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        if let Some(first) = first_translation {
            permissions_uniform &= translation.permissions == first.permissions;
            pat_index_uniform &= translation.pat_index == first.pat_index;
        } else {
            first_translation = Some(translation);
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    if let Some(first) = first_translation {
        kprintln!(
            "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages), first permissions={:?}, PAT index={}, leaf size={}, uniform permissions={}, uniform PAT index={}",
            label,
            pages,
            first.permissions,
            first.pat_index,
            first.page_size,
            permissions_uniform,
            pat_index_uniform
        );
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
    boot_info: &boot::BootInfo,
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    mtrrs: &rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    label: &str,
    kernel_virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} physical overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_virtual = match kernel_virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_virtual = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(address) => address,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM range: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, kernel_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, hhdm_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_translation.physical_address != physical
            || hhdm_translation.physical_address != physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias probe failed: {} physical {:#018x} has inconsistent translations",
                label,
                physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        let kernel_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            kernel_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            hhdm_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_type != hhdm_type {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias conflict: {} PA {:#018x}, kernel {:?} vs HHDM {:?}",
                label,
                physical,
                kernel_type,
                hhdm_type
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    kprintln!(
        "cache-alias probe passed: {} ({} pages; effective types match)",
        label,
        pages
    );
}

fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-page-fault")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately reads an unmapped
    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov rax, 0xdeadbeef",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately raises #UD; the
    // installed invalid-opcode handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("ud2", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

/// Set once the fatal panic path has started. A panic from inside the fatal
/// path stops silently instead of recursively printing or looping diagnostics.
static FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE: core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool =
    core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    // Mask maskable interrupts before any diagnostics run: another kernel
    // thread must not resume after a panic is declared, and the fatal report
    // must not be preempted mid-print.
    //
    // SAFETY: Kernel panic path runs at CPL 0; masking IF is always sound.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    if FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE.swap(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant panics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

+#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum KernelHalfValidationError<E> {
+    InvalidConfiguration,
+    InvalidRoot,
+    Reader(E),
+    UserAccessibleEntry {
+        level: u8,
+        index: u16,
+    },
+    InvalidEntry {
+        level: u8,
+        index: u16,
+    },
+    TableAliasedAcrossLevels {
+        physical_address: u64,
+        first_level: u8,
+        second_level: u8,
+    },
+    TableCapacityExceeded,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
+struct KernelTableVisit {
+    physical_address: u64,
+    level: u8,
+}
+
+impl KernelTableVisit {
+    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
+        physical_address: 0,
+        level: 0,
+    };
+}
+
+/// Validate every present mapping reachable from the upper-half root entries.
+///
+/// This bounded preflight rejects user-accessible entries at any level and
+/// malformed or out-of-width descendants before a kernel subtree is shared by
+/// process roots. Lower-half root entries are deliberately not inspected. The
+/// reader remains responsible for ensuring that every physical table read is
+/// authorized and safe.
+pub fn validate_supervisor_kernel_half<R: PageTableReader>(
+    reader: &R,
+    root: Cr3Root,
+    config: PageWalkConfig,
+) -> Result<usize, KernelHalfValidationError<R::Error>> {
+    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&config.physical_address_bits)
+        || (config.levels != 4 && config.levels != 5)
+        || config.virtual_address_bits != if config.levels == 4 { 48 } else { 57 }
+    {
+        return Err(KernelHalfValidationError::InvalidConfiguration);
+    }
+
+    let root_physical = root.physical_address();
+    let root_end = root_physical
+        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
+        .ok_or(KernelHalfValidationError::InvalidRoot)?;
+    if root_physical & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
+        || !physical_range_fits_address_width(root_physical, root_end, config.physical_address_bits)
+    {
+        return Err(KernelHalfValidationError::InvalidRoot);
+    }
+
+    const PRESENT: u64 = 1;
+    const USER: u64 = 1 << 2;
+    const PAGE_SIZE_OR_PAT: u64 = 1 << 7;
+    const NO_EXECUTE: u64 = 1 << 63;
+    const ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK: u64 = 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000;
+    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << config.physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
+
+    let mut visits = [KernelTableVisit::EMPTY; MAX_CANDIDATE_PAGE_TABLE_PAGES];
+    visits[0] = KernelTableVisit {
+        physical_address: root_physical,
+        level: config.levels,
+    };
+    let mut visit_count = 1usize;
+    let mut visit_index = 0usize;
+
+    while visit_index < visit_count {
+        let table = visits[visit_index];
+        let first_entry = if table.level == config.levels { 256 } else { 0 };
+        for index in first_entry..512 {
+            let index = index as u16;
+            let entry = reader
+                .read_entry(table.physical_address, index)
+                .map_err(KernelHalfValidationError::Reader)?;
+            if entry & PRESENT == 0 {
+                continue;
+            }
+            if entry & USER != 0 {
+                return Err(KernelHalfValidationError::UserAccessibleEntry {
+                    level: table.level,
+                    index,
+                });
+            }
+
+            let address_field = entry & ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK;
+            if address_field & !physical_mask != 0
+                || (!config.nx_enabled && entry & NO_EXECUTE != 0)
+            {
+                return Err(KernelHalfValidationError::InvalidEntry {
+                    level: table.level,
+                    index,
+                });
+            }
+

    30	### Process address spaces (design; not implemented)
    31	
    32	Use a separate four- or five-level root per process. The initial source is the retained active clone of Limine's hierarchy, not a curated clean-room root. Each process root owns its root page, all lower-half intermediate tables, and every user leaf frame. Keep the kernel-root owner alive for the lifetime of every process root. Copy only upper-half top-level entries from that owner into each process root; these entries are non-owning references to shared kernel subtrees, not deep copies, and must never be released by a process teardown. Do not copy lower-half entries from the kernel root.
    33	
    34	Before publishing a shared kernel subtree, validate its page-table structure and physical bounds and reject any present entry with the user/supervisor bit set at any level. `paging::validate_supervisor_kernel_half` implements this bounded preflight, but it does not install roots or prove physical backing is readable; the supplied reader must provide that access guarantee. Sharing the active clone means every accepted upper-half supervisor mapping and alias is present in every process CR3. This is not a curated kernel map or kernel-page-table isolation, and it provides no transient-execution protection. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.
    35	
    36	The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. Before releasing a process root or any of its user frames, switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate the local non-global translations; keep the shared kernel owner alive. Do not add PCID or SMP teardown/shootdown behavior implicitly: those require a separate design.
    37	
    38	The current `CandidatePageTables` deep-clones the inherited hierarchy, tracks all cloned table frames as owned, holds an exclusive mutable borrow of one memory backend, and does not provide shared-subtree ownership. It is not itself the process-address-space abstraction. Implement the shared-root policy in a distinct owner/handle API that can safely support multiple process roots without aliasing mutable backend references. //! Checked x86_64 mapping policy and a bounded owned page-table builder.
//!
//! Pure helpers validate addresses, permissions, and cache policy. Candidate
//! table access is delegated to an unsafe backend contract. This module never
//! writes CR3; callers may activate a validated hierarchy through the explicit
//! unsafe ownership marker after performing their architecture-specific switch.

use crate::frame::{Frame, FrameAllocator, FrameError};
use crate::memory::{
    is_canonical_virtual_address, physical_range_fits_address_width, HhdmAddressError, MemoryMap,
    RegionKind, ValidatedAcpiSpan, ValidatedMmioSpan,
};

/// Base page size supported by the initial Rustix mapping policy.
pub const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;

/// The physical root address and interpretation of CR3's low bits.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Cr3Root {
    physical_address: u64,
    low_bits: Cr3LowBits,
}

impl Cr3Root {
    pub const fn physical_address(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_address
    }

    pub const fn low_bits(self) -> Cr3LowBits {
        self.low_bits
    }
}

/// CR3's low bits are either a PCID or the paging-structure cache controls.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3LowBits {
    Pcid(u16),
    CacheControls {
        page_level_write_through: bool,
        page_level_cache_disable: bool,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3Error {
    UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidRootAddress,
    ReservedBits,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3RootAccessError {
    NotBootloaderReclaimable,
    Hhdm(HhdmAddressError),
}

/// Decode the currently active CR3 value without dereferencing its root table.
///
/// The caller supplies the reported physical-address width and whether CR4.PCIDE
/// is active, since those determine the valid address and low-bit encodings.
/// Encode a replacement CR3 value while preserving the active low-bit mode.
///
/// PCID is retained but the no-flush bit is always cleared so the selected PCID
/// is invalidated on load. Legacy PWT/PCD controls are preserved unchanged.
pub fn encode_cr3_value(
    root_physical_address: u64,
    low_bits: Cr3LowBits,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<u64, Cr3Error> {
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }
    let root_end = root_physical_address
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(Cr3Error::InvalidRootAddress)?;
    if root_physical_address & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
        || !physical_range_fits_address_width(
            root_physical_address,
            root_end,
            physical_address_bits,
        )
    {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidRootAddress);
    }
    let low = match low_bits {
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid(pcid) if pcid <= 0x0fff => u64::from(pcid),
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid(_) => return Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits),
        Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
            page_level_write_through,
            page_level_cache_disable,
        } => {
            (u64::from(page_level_write_through) << 3) | (u64::from(page_level_cache_disable) << 4)
        }
    };
    Ok(root_physical_address | low)
}

pub fn parse_cr3_root(
    raw: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    pcid_enabled: bool,
) -> Result<Cr3Root, Cr3Error> {
    let physical_address_bits =
        physical_address_bits.ok_or(Cr3Error::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)?;
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }

    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    let low_mask = if pcid_enabled {
        PAGE_SIZE - 1
    } else {
        (1 << 3) | (1 << 4)
    };
    if raw & !(physical_mask | low_mask) != 0 {
        return Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits);
    }

    let low_bits = if pcid_enabled {
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid((raw & (PAGE_SIZE - 1)) as u16)
    } else {
        Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
            page_level_write_through: raw & (1 << 3) != 0,
            page_level_cache_disable: raw & (1 << 4) != 0,
        }
    };

    Ok(Cr3Root {
        physical_address: raw & physical_mask,
        low_bits,
    })
}

/// Calculate the protocol-backed HHDM address of Limine's inherited root page.
///
/// This requires the root page to be wholly contained in bootloader-reclaimable
/// memory, as specified for Limine page tables. It does not dereference the page
/// or prove that the active hierarchy contains the HHDM mapping.
pub fn inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
    root: Cr3Root,
    memory_map: &MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<u64, Cr3RootAccessError> {
    let physical_start = root.physical_address();
    let physical_end = physical_start
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(Cr3RootAccessError::Hhdm(HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow))?;
    if !memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
        physical_start,
        physical_end,
        RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
    ) {
        return Err(Cr3RootAccessError::NotBootloaderReclaimable);
    }
    memory_map
        .limine_hhdm_address(
            hhdm_offset,
            physical_start,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            physical_address_bits,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
        .map_err(Cr3RootAccessError::Hhdm)
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageLevel {
    Pml5,
    Pml4,
    Pdpt,
    Pd,
    Pt,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageWalkConfig {
    pub levels: u8,
    pub physical_address_bits: u8,
    pub virtual_address_bits: u8,
    pub nx_enabled: bool,
    pub page_2m_supported: bool,
    pub page_1g_supported: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageTranslation {
    pub physical_address: u64,
    pub leaf_physical_base: u64,
    pub page_size: u64,
    pub permissions: PagePermissions,
    pub pat_index: u8,
    pub raw_leaf_entry: u64,
}

impl PageTranslation {
    /// Compare effective mapping policy while allowing equivalent large-page splits.
    ///
    /// Physical address, permissions, PAT index, global/software flags, and
    /// other stable leaf attributes must match. Leaf size, physical base, and
    /// hardware-maintained accessed/dirty bits may differ after a page split.
    pub const fn same_effective_mapping(self, other: Self) -> bool {
        const IGNORED_LEAF_BITS: u64 = PTE_ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK | (1 << 5) | (1 << 6) | (1 << 7);

        self.physical_address == other.physical_address
            && self.permissions.writable == other.permissions.writable
            && self.permissions.executable == other.permissions.executable
            && self.permissions.user_accessible == other.permissions.user_accessible
            && self.pat_index == other.pat_index
            && self.raw_leaf_entry & !IGNORED_LEAF_BITS == other.raw_leaf_entry & !IGNORED_LEAF_BITS
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageWalkOutcome {
    NotPresent { level: PageLevel },
    Mapped(PageTranslation),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageTableEntryError {
    PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
    NxDisabled,
    LargePageUnsupported,
    LargePageAtInvalidLevel,
    LargePageMisaligned,
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageWalkError<E> {
    InvalidConfiguration,
    NonCanonicalAddress,
    InvalidRoot,
    InvalidEntry {
        level: PageLevel,
        error: PageTableEntryError,
    },
    Reader(E),
}

/// Read one raw entry from a table at a validated physical page address.
pub trait PageTableReader {
    type Error;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error>;
}

/// Translate one virtual address by following at most five page-table entries.
///
/// The reader owns all physical-memory access policy. This walker does not turn
/// physical addresses into pointers, modify tables, or infer effective cache
/// types from the leaf PAT selector.
pub fn walk_virtual_address<R: PageTableReader>(
    reader: &R,
    root: Cr3Root,
    virtual_address: u64,
    config: PageWalkConfig,
) -> Result<PageWalkOutcome, PageWalkError<R::Error>> {
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&config.physical_address_bits)
        || (config.levels != 4 && config.levels != 5)
        || config.virtual_address_bits != if config.levels == 4 { 48 } else { 57 }
    {
        return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidConfiguration);
    }
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_address, config.virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(PageWalkError::NonCanonicalAddress);
    }
    let root_physical = root.physical_address();
    let root_end = root_physical
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(PageWalkError::InvalidRoot)?;
    if root_physical & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
        || !physical_range_fits_address_width(root_physical, root_end, config.physical_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidRoot);
    }

    const PRESENT: u64 = 1;
    const WRITABLE: u64 = 1 << 1;
    const USER: u64 = 1 << 2;
    const WRITE_THROUGH: u64 = 1 << 3;
    const CACHE_DISABLE: u64 = 1 << 4;
    const PAGE_SIZE_OR_PAT: u64 = 1 << 7;
    const LARGE_PAGE_PAT: u64 = 1 << 12;
    const NO_EXECUTE: u64 = 1 << 63;
    const ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK: u64 = 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000;

    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << config.physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    let mut table_physical = root_physical;
    let mut writable = true;
    let mut user_accessible = true;
    let mut executable = true;
    let mut level_number = config.levels;

    loop {
        let shift = 12 + 9 * (level_number - 1);
        let index = ((virtual_address >> shift) & 0x1ff) as u16;
        let entry = reader
            .read_entry(table_physical, index)
            .map_err(PageWalkError::Reader)?;
        let level = match level_number {
            5 => PageLevel::Pml5,
            4 => PageLevel::Pml4,
            3 => PageLevel::Pdpt,
            2 => PageLevel::Pd,
            1 => PageLevel::Pt,
            _ => return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidConfiguration),
        };
        if entry & PRESENT == 0 {
            return Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level });
        }

        let address_field = entry & ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK;
        if address_field & !physical_mask != 0 {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
            });
        }
        if !config.nx_enabled && entry & NO_EXECUTE != 0 {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::NxDisabled,
            });
        }
        writable &= entry & WRITABLE != 0;
        user_accessible &= entry & USER != 0;
        executable &= entry & NO_EXECUTE == 0;

        let large_page = level_number > 1 && entry & PAGE_SIZE_OR_PAT != 0;
        let leaf_shift = if level_number == 1 {
            12
        } else if large_page && level_number == 2 && config.page_2m_supported {
            21
        } else if large_page && level_number == 3 && config.page_1g_supported {
            30
        } else if large_page && level_number <= 3 {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::LargePageUnsupported,
            });
        } else if large_page {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::LargePageAtInvalidLevel,
            });
        } else {
            table_physical = address_field;
            level_number -= 1;
            continue;
        };

        if large_page {
            let reserved_alignment_bits = ((1u64 << leaf_shift) - 1) & !0x1fff;
            if entry & reserved_alignment_bits != 0 {
                return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                    level,
                    error: PageTableEntryError::LargePageMisaligned,
                });
            }
        }
        let page_size = 1u64 << leaf_shift;
        let leaf_physical_base = address_field & !(page_size - 1);
        let leaf_physical_end =
            leaf_physical_base
                .checked_add(page_size)
                .ok_or(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                    level,
                    error: PageTableEntryError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
                })?;
        if !physical_range_fits_address_width(
            leaf_physical_base,
            leaf_physical_end,
            config.physical_address_bits,
        ) {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
            });
        }
        let pat_bit = if large_page {
            entry & LARGE_PAGE_PAT != 0
        } else {
            entry & PAGE_SIZE_OR_PAT != 0
        };
        let pat_index = (u8::from(pat_bit) << 2)
            | (u8::from(entry & CACHE_DISABLE != 0) << 1)
            | u8::from(entry & WRITE_THROUGH != 0);
        return Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
            physical_address: leaf_physical_base | (virtual_address & (page_size - 1)),
            leaf_physical_base,
            page_size,
            permissions: PagePermissions {
                writable,
                executable,
                user_accessible,
            },
            pat_index,
            raw_leaf_entry: entry,
        }));
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum KernelHalfValidationError<E> {
    InvalidConfiguration,
    InvalidRoot,
    Reader(E),
    UserAccessibleEntry {
        level: u8,
        index: u16,
    },
    InvalidEntry {
        level: u8,
        index: u16,
    },
    TableAliasedAcrossLevels {
        physical_address: u64,
        first_level: u8,
        second_level: u8,
    },
    TableCapacityExceeded,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct KernelTableVisit {
    physical_address: u64,
    level: u8,
    user_accessible: bool,
}

impl KernelTableVisit {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        physical_address: 0,
        level: 0,
        user_accessible: false,
    };
}

/// Validate every present mapping reachable from the upper-half root entries.
///
/// This bounded preflight rejects mappings that are effectively user-accessible
/// at a leaf, plus malformed or out-of-width descendants, before a kernel subtree
/// is shared by process roots. U/S bits on individual non-leaf entries are not
/// sufficient to grant user access; the effective permission is the AND of all
/// entries on the path. Lower-half root entries are deliberately not inspected.
/// The reader remains responsible for ensuring that every physical table read
/// is authorized and safe.
pub fn validate_supervisor_kernel_half<R: PageTableReader>(
    reader: &R,
    root: Cr3Root,
    config: PageWalkConfig,
) -> Result<usize, KernelHalfValidationError<R::Error>> {
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&config.physical_address_bits)
        || (config.levels != 4 && config.levels != 5)
        || config.virtual_address_bits != if config.levels == 4 { 48 } else { 57 }
    {
        return Err(KernelHalfValidationError::InvalidConfiguration);
    }

    let root_physical = root.physical_address();
    let root_end = root_physical
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(KernelHalfValidationError::InvalidRoot)?;
    if root_physical & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
        || !physical_range_fits_address_width(root_physical, root_end, config.physical_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(KernelHalfValidationError::InvalidRoot);
    }

    const PRESENT: u64 = 1;
    const USER: u64 = 1 << 2;
    const PAGE_SIZE_OR_PAT: u64 = 1 << 7;
    const NO_EXECUTE: u64 = 1 << 63;
    const ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK: u64 = 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000;
    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << config.physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);

    let mut visits = [KernelTableVisit::EMPTY; MAX_CANDIDATE_PAGE_TABLE_PAGES * 2];
    visits[0] = KernelTableVisit {
        physical_address: root_physical,
        level: config.levels,
        user_accessible: true,
    };
    let mut visit_count = 1usize;
    let mut unique_table_count = 1usize;
    let mut visit_index = 0usize;

    while visit_index < visit_count {
        let table = visits[visit_index];
        let first_entry = if table.level == config.levels { 256 } else { 0 };
        for index in first_entry..512 {
            let index = index as u16;
            let entry = reader
                .read_entry(table.physical_address, index)
                .map_err(KernelHalfValidationError::Reader)?;
            if entry & PRESENT == 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let user_accessible = table.user_accessible && entry & USER != 0;
            let address_field = entry & ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK;
            if address_field & !physical_mask != 0
                || (!config.nx_enabled && entry & NO_EXECUTE != 0)
            {
                return Err(KernelHalfValidationError::InvalidEntry {
                    level: table.level,
                    index,
                });
            }

            let large_page = table.level > 1 && entry & PAGE_SIZE_OR_PAT != 0;
            if table.level == 1 || large_page {
                let page_size = if table.level == 1 {
                    PAGE_SIZE
                } else {
                    match table.level {
                        2 if config.page_2m_supported => 1 << 21,
                        3 if config.page_1g_supported => 1 << 30,
                        _ => {
                            return Err(KernelHalfValidationError::InvalidEntry {
                                level: table.level,
                                index,
                            });
                        }
                    }
                };
                if large_page {
                    let reserved_alignment_bits = (page_size - 1) & !0x1fff;
                    if entry & reserved_alignment_bits != 0 {
                        return Err(KernelHalfValidationError::InvalidEntry {
                            level: table.level,
                            index,
                        });
                    }
                }
                let physical_start = address_field & !(page_size - 1);
                let physical_end = physical_start.checked_add(page_size).ok_or(
                    KernelHalfValidationError::InvalidEntry {
                        level: table.level,
                        index,
                    },
                )?;
                if !physical_range_fits_address_width(
                    physical_start,
                    physical_end,
                    config.physical_address_bits,
                ) {
                    return Err(KernelHalfValidationError::InvalidEntry {
                        level: table.level,
                        index,
                    });
                }
                if user_accessible {
                    return Err(KernelHalfValidationError::UserAccessibleEntry {
                        level: table.level,
                        index,
                    });
                }
                continue;
            }

            let child_level = table.level - 1;
            let child_end = address_field.checked_add(PAGE_SIZE).ok_or(
                KernelHalfValidationError::InvalidEntry {
                    level: table.level,
                    index,
                },
            )?;
            if !physical_range_fits_address_width(
                address_field,
                child_end,
                config.physical_address_bits,
            ) {
                return Err(KernelHalfValidationError::InvalidEntry {
                    level: table.level,
                    index,
                });
            }
            let existing = visits[..visit_count]
                .iter()
                .find(|visit| visit.physical_address == address_field);
            if let Some(existing) = existing {
                if existing.level != child_level {
                    return Err(KernelHalfValidationError::TableAliasedAcrossLevels {
                        physical_address: address_field,
                        first_level: existing.level,
                        second_level: child_level,
                    });
                }
                if existing.user_accessible == user_accessible {
                    continue;
                }
            } else {
                if unique_table_count == MAX_CANDIDATE_PAGE_TABLE_PAGES {
                    return Err(KernelHalfValidationError::TableCapacityExceeded);
                }
                unique_table_count += 1;
            }
            if visit_count == visits.len() {
                return Err(KernelHalfValidationError::TableCapacityExceeded);
            }
            visits[visit_count] = KernelTableVisit {
                physical_address: address_field,
                level: child_level,
                user_accessible,
            };
            visit_count += 1;
        }
        visit_index += 1;
    }

    Ok(unique_table_count)
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PagePermissions {
    pub writable: bool,
    pub executable: bool,
    pub user_accessible: bool,
}

/// A mapping range whose arithmetic, address widths, alignment, and W^X policy passed validation.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ValidatedMappingRange {
    virtual_start: u64,
    virtual_end: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    physical_end: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    permissions: PagePermissions,
}

/// PAT selection for one physical extent, derived from supplied PAT/MTRR state.
///
/// This records a uniform effective type across the range, but does not inspect
/// existing mappings or prove that aliases use compatible cache attributes.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SelectedCacheAttributes {
    physical_start: u64,
    physical_end: u64,
    pat_index: u8,
    effective_type: EffectiveMemoryType,
}

impl SelectedCacheAttributes {
    pub const fn physical_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_start
    }

    pub const fn physical_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_end
    }

    pub const fn pat_index(self) -> u8 {
        self.pat_index
    }

    pub const fn effective_type(self) -> EffectiveMemoryType {
        self.effective_type
    }
}

impl ValidatedMappingRange {
    pub const fn virtual_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_start
    }

    pub const fn virtual_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_end
    }

    pub const fn physical_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_start
    }

    pub const fn physical_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_end
    }

    pub const fn permissions(self) -> PagePermissions {
        self.permissions
    }

    pub const fn length(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_end - self.virtual_start
    }

    /// Select PAT attributes that yield one effective type across this range.
    ///
    /// The supplied PAT/MTRR snapshot and `normal_caching` flag must reflect the
    /// active hardware state. This is a policy calculation only; it does not
    /// inspect existing mappings or detect cache-type aliases.
    pub fn select_cache_attributes(
        self,
        policy: CachePolicy,
        pat: PatLayout,
        mtrrs: &ValidatedMtrrLayout,
        normal_caching: bool,
    ) -> Result<SelectedCacheAttributes, MappingError> {
        if self.physical_address_bits != mtrrs.physical_address_bits {
            return Err(MappingError::MtrrPhysicalAddressWidthMismatch);
        }

        let effective_type = match policy {
            CachePolicy::WriteBack => EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack,
            CachePolicy::Uncacheable => EffectiveMemoryType::Uncacheable,
            CachePolicy::WriteCombining => EffectiveMemoryType::WriteCombining,
        };
        let pat_index = mtrrs
            .select_pat_index_for_range(
                self.physical_start,
                self.length(),
                pat,
                effective_type,
                normal_caching,
            )
            .map_err(MappingError::CachePolicy)?;

        Ok(SelectedCacheAttributes {
            physical_start: self.physical_start,
            physical_end: self.physical_end,
            pat_index,
            effective_type,
        })
    }

    /// Encode a 4 KiB leaf PTE using attributes selected for this physical range.
    pub fn leaf_4k_entry_with_cache_attributes(
        self,
        page_offset: u64,
        cache_attributes: SelectedCacheAttributes,
        nx_enabled: bool,
    ) -> Result<PageTableEntry, MappingError> {
        if cache_attributes.physical_start != self.physical_start
            || cache_attributes.physical_end != self.physical_end
        {
            return Err(MappingError::CacheAttributesRangeMismatch);
        }
        self.leaf_4k_entry(page_offset, cache_attributes.pat_index, nx_enabled)
    }

    /// Encode a single 4 KiB leaf PTE within this validated range.
    ///
    /// `pat_index` is the raw three-bit PAT index; the caller must have verified
    /// that the active PAT MSR gives it the intended cache semantics. `nx_enabled`
    /// must reflect EFER.NXE, not merely CPUID support. This only creates entry
    /// bits—it neither owns the frame nor writes a page table.
    pub fn leaf_4k_entry(
        self,
        page_offset: u64,
        pat_index: u8,
        nx_enabled: bool,
    ) -> Result<PageTableEntry, MappingError> {
        if page_offset & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(MappingError::UnalignedPageOffset);
        }
        if page_offset >= self.length() {
            return Err(MappingError::PageOffsetOutOfRange);
        }
        if self.physical_address_bits > MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS {
            return Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
        }
        if pat_index > 7 {
            return Err(MappingError::InvalidPatIndex);
        }
        if !self.permissions.executable && !nx_enabled {
            return Err(MappingError::NxNotEnabled);
        }

        let physical_address = self
            .physical_start
            .checked_add(page_offset)
            .ok_or(MappingError::AddressOverflow)?;
        let mut bits = physical_address | PTE_PRESENT;
        if self.permissions.writable {
            bits |= PTE_WRITABLE;
        }
        if self.permissions.user_accessible {
            bits |= PTE_USER;
        }
        if pat_index & 0b001 != 0 {
            bits |= PTE_WRITE_THROUGH;
        }
        if pat_index & 0b010 != 0 {
            bits |= PTE_CACHE_DISABLE;
        }
        if pat_index & 0b100 != 0 {
            bits |= PTE_PAT_4K;
        }
        if !self.permissions.executable {
            bits |= PTE_NO_EXECUTE;
        }

        Ok(PageTableEntry(bits))
    }
}

/// Maximum x86_64 physical-address width representable by a 4 KiB PTE.
pub const MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS: u8 = 52;
const PTE_PRESENT: u64 = 1 << 0;
const PTE_WRITABLE: u64 = 1 << 1;
const PTE_USER: u64 = 1 << 2;
const PTE_WRITE_THROUGH: u64 = 1 << 3;
const PTE_CACHE_DISABLE: u64 = 1 << 4;
const PTE_ACCESSED: u64 = 1 << 5;
const PTE_PAT_4K: u64 = 1 << 7;
const PTE_NO_EXECUTE: u64 = 1 << 63;

/// Raw bits for one x86_64 4 KiB leaf page-table entry.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageTableEntry(u64);

impl PageTableEntry {
    pub const fn bits(self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CachePolicy {
    WriteBack,
    Uncacheable,
    WriteCombining,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PatMemoryType {
    Uncacheable,
    WriteCombining,
    WriteThrough,
    WriteProtected,
    WriteBack,
    UncacheableMinus,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EffectiveMemoryType {
    Uncacheable,
    WriteCombining,
    WriteThrough,
    WriteProtected,
    WriteBack,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PatLayoutError {
    ReservedBits { index: u8 },
    ReservedMemoryType { index: u8, value: u8 },
}

/// Parsed PAT memory types from an `IA32_PAT` MSR value supplied by the caller.
///
/// Parsing does not read the MSR or establish that this is the active value. The
/// MTRR configuration may also affect the effective cache type for an address.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PatLayout {
    memory_types: [u8; 8],
}

impl PatLayout {
    pub fn from_msr_value(value: u64) -> Result<Self, PatLayoutError> {
        let mut memory_types = [0; 8];
        for (index, memory_type) in memory_types.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            let entry = ((value >> (index * 8)) & 0xff) as u8;
            if entry & !0x07 != 0 {
                return Err(PatLayoutError::ReservedBits { index: index as u8 });
            }
            if entry == 0b010 || entry == 0b011 {
                return Err(PatLayoutError::ReservedMemoryType {
                    index: index as u8,
                    value: entry,
                });
            }
            *memory_type = entry;
        }
        Ok(Self { memory_types })
    }

    /// Return the first PAT index with the exact requested memory type.
    pub fn index_for(self, policy: CachePolicy) -> Option<u8> {
        let requested_type = match policy {
            CachePolicy::Uncacheable => 0b000,
            CachePolicy::WriteCombining => 0b001,
            CachePolicy::WriteBack => 0b110,
        };
        self.memory_types
            .iter()
            .position(|memory_type| *memory_type == requested_type)
            .map(|index| index as u8)
    }

    fn memory_type_at(self, index: u8) -> Result<PatMemoryType, EffectiveMemoryTypeError> {
        match self.memory_types.get(usize::from(index)).copied() {
            Some(0) => Ok(PatMemoryType::Uncacheable),
            Some(1) => Ok(PatMemoryType::WriteCombining),
            Some(4) => Ok(PatMemoryType::WriteThrough),
            Some(5) => Ok(PatMemoryType::WriteProtected),
            Some(6) => Ok(PatMemoryType::WriteBack),
            Some(7) => Ok(PatMemoryType::UncacheableMinus),
            Some(_) => unreachable!("PAT layouts reject reserved memory types"),
            None => Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::PatIndexOutOfRange { index }),
        }
    }
}

const IA32_MTRRCAP: u32 = 0x0000_00fe;
const IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE: u32 = 0x0000_02ff;
const IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0: u32 = 0x0000_0200;
const MTRRCAP_FIXED_SUPPORTED: u64 = 1 << 8;
const MTRRCAP_PRMRR_SUPPORTED: u64 = 1 << 12; // Recognized but not consumed by this MTRR policy.
const MTRRCAP_KNOWN_BITS: u64 = 0x0dff | MTRRCAP_PRMRR_SUPPORTED;
const FIXED_MTRR_REGISTER_INDICES: [u32; 11] = [
    0x250, 0x258, 0x259, 0x268, 0x269, 0x26a, 0x26b, 0x26c, 0x26d, 0x26e, 0x26f,
];

/// Maximum variable MTRR pairs retained in the fixed-capacity boot snapshot.
pub const MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS: usize = 32;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MtrrRegisterPair {
    pub base: u64,
    pub mask: u64,
}

/// Raw MTRR state captured for diagnostics; values still require policy validation.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MtrrRegisters {
    pub capability: u64,
    pub default_type: u64,
    pub fixed_registers: Option<[u64; 11]>,
    pub variable_register_count: u8,
    pub variable_registers: [MtrrRegisterPair; MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS],
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MtrrState {
    Unsupported,
    VariableRangeCapacityExceeded { reported_count: u8 },
    Captured(MtrrRegisters),
}

/// Capture a bounded register snapshot using a caller-provided MSR reader.
///
/// This helper performs no hardware access itself. A false support flag returns
/// without invoking the reader; an over-capacity count returns no partial data.
pub fn capture_mtrr_registers(supported: bool, mut read_msr: impl FnMut(u32) -> u64) -> MtrrState {
    if !supported {
        return MtrrState::Unsupported;
    }

    let capability = read_msr(IA32_MTRRCAP);
    let variable_register_count = (capability & 0xff) as u8;
    if usize::from(variable_register_count) > MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS {
        return MtrrState::VariableRangeCapacityExceeded {
            reported_count: variable_register_count,
        };
    }

    let default_type = read_msr(IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE);
    let fixed_registers = if capability & MTRRCAP_FIXED_SUPPORTED != 0 {
        let mut registers = [0; FIXED_MTRR_REGISTER_INDICES.len()];
        for (register, index) in registers.iter_mut().zip(FIXED_MTRR_REGISTER_INDICES) {
            *register = read_msr(index);
        }
        Some(registers)
    } else {
        None
    };

    let mut variable_registers =
        [MtrrRegisterPair { base: 0, mask: 0 }; MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS];
    for (range_index, registers) in variable_registers
        .iter_mut()
        .take(usize::from(variable_register_count))
        .enumerate()
    {
        let base_index = IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0 + 2 * range_index as u32;
        registers.base = read_msr(base_index);
        registers.mask = read_msr(base_index + 1);
    }

    MtrrState::Captured(MtrrRegisters {
        capability,
        default_type,
        fixed_registers,
        variable_register_count,
        variable_registers,
    })
}

pub const FIXED_MTRR_TYPE_COUNT: usize = 88;
const MAX_MTRR_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS: u8 = 52;
const MTRR_VALID: u64 = 1 << 11;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum MtrrMemoryType {
    Uncacheable = 0,
    WriteCombining = 1,
    WriteThrough = 4,
    WriteProtected = 5,
    WriteBack = 6,
}

impl MtrrMemoryType {
    pub fn from_raw(value: u8) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
        match value {
            0 => Ok(Self::Uncacheable),
            1 => Ok(Self::WriteCombining),
            4 => Ok(Self::WriteThrough),
            5 => Ok(Self::WriteProtected),
            6 => Ok(Self::WriteBack),
            value => Err(MtrrError::ReservedMemoryType { value }),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MtrrError {
    InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth,
    ReservedCapabilityBits,
    ReservedDefaultTypeBits,
    ReservedBaseBits,
    ReservedMaskBits,
    UnsupportedDiscontinuousVariableMask,
    MisalignedVariableBase,
    InvalidVariableRange,
    ReservedMemoryType { value: u8 },
    FixedRangesUnavailable,
    FixedRegisterSupportMismatch,
    VariableRegisterCountMismatch,
    WriteCombiningUnsupported,
    PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
    PhysicalAddressWidthMismatch,
    UndefinedOverlap,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EffectiveMemoryTypeError {
    Mtrr(MtrrError),
    PatIndexOutOfRange { index: u8 },
    NonNormalCachingMode,
    EmptyRange,
    UnalignedRange,
    AddressOverflow,
    NoUniformPatIndex { requested: EffectiveMemoryType },
}

/// Decoded fixed MTRR memory types in ascending physical-address order.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FixedMtrrRanges {
    memory_types: [MtrrMemoryType; FIXED_MTRR_TYPE_COUNT],
}

impl FixedMtrrRanges {
    /// Decode FIX64K_00000, FIX16K_80000/A0000, and FIX4K_C0000..F8000.
    pub fn from_msr_values(registers: [u64; 11]) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
